definition_zh: 装饰；装点
definition_en: to decorate someone or something, especially richly or showily
core_image: 节日街道挂满彩灯与花环
scene: 新年将至，街道挂满灯笼与花环。 The old town was bedecked with lanterns for the festival.
sceneCN: 这里 bedecked 是「被装点」（第 1 个义项：以饰物装扮、布置）；句意是古镇为节庆挂满灯笼。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「装饰；打扮」（deck out）
由过去分词转形容词，义为「装饰过的；挂满饰物的」
由现在分词转名词，义为「装饰；装点」

senses.title: To decorate richly
senses.definition: to adorn someone or something with ornaments
senses.definitionCN: 以饰物装扮人或物
senses.example: The old town was bedecked with lanterns for the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 古镇为节庆挂满灯笼。
senses.why: The be- prefix makes the decoration cover the object completely.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 be- 表示装饰把对象整个覆盖。

senses.title: To adorn oneself showily
senses.definition: to dress oneself up, often in a showy way
senses.definitionCN: 为自己盛装打扮，常带炫耀意味
senses.example: She bedecked herself in jewels before the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 舞会前她满身珠宝盛装打扮。
senses.why: The covering idea turns inward, as the person becomes the ornamented object.
senses.whyCN: 「覆盖」意象转向自身，人成为被装饰的对象。

intro.en: Bedeck adds be- to deck, itself from Dutch covering cloth.
intro.cn: bedeck 在 deck 前加 be-；deck 源于荷兰语中覆盖的布。

items.en: decken meant to cover or spread.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 decken 意为「覆盖、铺开」。

items.en: deck meant to clothe or adorn.
items.cn: 中古英语 deck 意为「给……穿衣、打扮」。

items.en: bedeck appeared as an intensified form.
items.cn: 十六世纪 bedeck 作为强化形式出现。

items.en: deck out kept the sense of dressing up.
items.cn: deck out 保留「盛装打扮」之义。

items.en: bedecked with is now the most common pattern.
items.cn: 如今 bedecked with 是最常见搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- prefix or the deck root; the near-meaning group gathers words for adorning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 be- 前缀或 deck 词根；近义组汇集装饰类词。

entries.definition: to decorate or dress up
entries.definitionCN: 装饰；打扮——bedeck 的基础词

entries.definition: to smear messily
entries.definitionCN: 乱涂；同前缀而意义相反方向

entries.definition: a signal light
entries.definitionCN: 信标；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to add beauty to
entries.definitionCN: 装饰；强调增添美感

entries.definition: to decorate with ornaments
entries.definitionCN: 装点；强调以饰品点缀

entries.definition: to crown with a wreath of flowers
entries.definitionCN: 戴花环；一种具体装饰方式

normalIntro.en: Bedeck is deck with be-: deck it out fully.
normalIntro.cn: bedeck 是 deck 加 be-：把装饰做足。

normal.en: Deck alone can mean to decorate.
normal.cn: deck 单独用可指「装饰」。

normal.en: Deck out means to dress up richly.
normal.cn: deck out 指盛装打扮。

normal.en: Bedecked with flowers is the classic phrase.
normal.cn: bedecked with flowers 是经典搭配。

normal.en: One can bedeck oneself in jewels.
normal.cn: 可以说 bedeck oneself in jewels。

normal.en: The deck of a ship is a different sense, a covering.
normal.cn: 船的甲板是 deck 的另一义，指「覆盖面」。

abstract.en: See lanterns strung across an old street.
abstract.cn: 想象灯笼挂满老街。

abstract.en: Feel silk and cold jewels at your throat.
abstract.cn: 感受丝缎与颈间冰凉的珠宝。

abstract.en: Picture a plain room turned brilliant.
abstract.cn: 想象朴素的房间焕然生辉。

examples.en: The old town was bedecked with lanterns for the festival.
examples.cn: 古镇为节庆挂满灯笼。

examples.en: She bedecked herself in jewels before the ball.
examples.cn: 舞会前她满身珠宝盛装打扮。

examples.en: Streets bedecked with flags welcomed the returning team.
examples.cn: 挂满旗帜的街道迎接归来的队伍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「比·戴克」——比赛谁戴得克丽夺目，就是「盛装装饰」。

root: 前缀 be-（古英语，表「使、覆盖」）加 deck；deck 源自中古荷兰语 decken「覆盖」，经中古英语先指「穿衣」，再转指「打扮、装饰」，十六世纪与 be- 结合成为 bedeck。

sensesIntro.en: One verb drapes decoration over streets and over oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个动词，把装饰披上街道，也披上自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lanterns and garlands covering an old street.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯笼花环覆满老街。

intro.en: Bedeck joins the be- covering family, the bright twin of bedaub.
intro.cn: bedeck 属于 be- 覆盖家族，是 bedaub 光鲜的孪生词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the root is Middle Dutch decken.

definition_zh: 响尾蛇；[喻] 阴险的人、暗藏危险者
definition_en: a poisonous snake that shakes its tail to make a rattling warning
core_image: 沙地上一段盘起的身体，尾巴抬起，发出干燥的沙沙声
scene: 沙地上一条蛇抬起尾端，干燥的响声先于它的动作出现。 On the sand a rattlesnake lifted its tail, and the dry sound came before any movement.
sceneCN: 这里 rattlesnake 指响尾蛇（第 1 个义项：会摇尾发声的蛇）；句意为沙地上一条响尾蛇抬起尾端，干燥的响声先于它的动作出现。

senses.title: The snake and its rattle
senses.definition: a venomous American snake whose jointed tail rattles as a warning before it strikes
senses.definitionCN: 一种美洲毒蛇，尾端有环节，在攻击之前摇动发声以示警告
senses.example: On the sand a rattlesnake lifted its tail, and the dry sound came before any movement.
senses.exampleCN: 沙地上一条响尾蛇抬起尾端，干燥的响声先于它的动作出现。
senses.why: The name is the animal and the sound together: rattle plus snake, a warning built into the body.
senses.whyCN: 名字把动物和声音合在一起：rattle 加 snake，警告器长在身体里。

senses.title: A treacherous person
senses.definition: a person who gives friendly signals and strikes anyway, or hides a threat under a calm manner
senses.definitionCN: 发出友善信号却照样下手的人，或把危险藏在温和外表下的人
senses.example: He was a rattlesnake in negotiations, smiling before he bit.
senses.exampleCN: 他在谈判中像条响尾蛇，咬人之前还先笑。
senses.why: The figure keeps the warning and drops the mercy, and that is where the insult lies.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻留下警告、丢掉仁慈，侮辱性正来自这里：会响，却照样咬。

intro.en: Rattlesnake is an English compound of rattle and snake, named for the sound of its tail.
intro.cn: rattlesnake 是 rattle 与 snake 的英语复合词，因尾部声响得名。

items.en: Rattle first meant to make a quick knocking sound.
items.cn: rattle 最初指发出急促敲击声。

items.en: Snake has named the animal since Old English.
items.cn: snake 自古英语起就指这种动物。

items.en: Settlers in America named the species by its noise.
items.cn: 美洲移民按它的声响为这个物种命名。

items.en: Naturalists fixed the compound in print.
items.cn: 博物学家把这个复合词固定进书里。

items.en: Writers borrowed it for a treacherous person.
items.cn: 作家借它指阴险的人。

note.en: The look-alike group is the rattle- family; the near-meaning group separates viper, copperhead, adder and serpent.
note.cn: 形近组是 rattle 词族；近义组把「蝰蛇」「铜头蛇」「毒蛇」「巨蛇」分开。

entries.definition: to make a quick knocking sound.

entries.definition: making a knocking sound.
entries.definitionCN: 发出敲击声的。

entries.definition: nervous or shaken.

entries.definition: the skin of a snake.

entries.definitionCN: 一种小毒蛇。

entries.definition: a large snake, often figurative.
entries.definitionCN: 大蛇，常用于比喻。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a tail lifted on sand and a dry sound arriving first.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「沙地上抬起的尾巴，干燥的响声先到」的画面。

normal.en: Rattlesnake is rattle plus snake: the name is the sound.
normal.cn: rattlesnake 是 rattle 加 snake：名字就是那个声音。

normal.en: Picture a warning arriving before the body moves.
normal.cn: 想象警告先于身体的动作到达。

normal.en: Say RAT-l-snayk; the middle is thin and quick.
normal.cn: 读 RAT-l-snayk，中间又薄又快。

normal.en: The metaphor keeps the warning and drops the mercy.
normal.cn: 这个比喻留下警告，丢掉仁慈。

normal.en: Ask whether a warning is kindness or a threat made polite.
normal.cn: 问一句：警告是善意，还是被说得客气的威胁？

abstract.en: A rattlesnake is danger with a public address system.
abstract.cn: 响尾蛇是装了广播的危险。

abstract.en: The sound is a contract: I have told you, so what follows is your choice.
abstract.cn: 那声音是一份契约：我已经告诉你了，接下来的就是你的选择。

abstract.en: The word teaches that warnings are only mercy when the striker can be avoided.
abstract.cn: 这个词教人：只有攻击能被避开时，警告才算仁慈。

examples.en: The rattlesnake's rattle is a warning, and a warning is a kind of mercy.
examples.cn: 响尾蛇的尾响是一种警告，而警告也是一种仁慈。

examples.en: He was a rattlesnake in negotiations, smiling before he bit.
examples.cn: 他在谈判中像条响尾蛇，咬人之前还先笑。

examples.en: A rattlesnake gives a warning you can hear before it strikes.
examples.cn: 响尾蛇在攻击之前，会给出一个你听得见的警告。

root: 英语 rattle（急促响声）+ snake（蛇）

sensesIntro.en: Rattlesnake has two senses: the animal with a built-in warning, and the person whose courtesy hides a strike.
sensesIntro.cn: 响尾蛇有两层：带着天生警报器的动物，以及用客气藏起攻击的人。

branches.en: A dry sound crossing open sand.

intro.cn: rattle 词族建立在声音上：rattle、rattling、rattled、rattlesnake 都从急促的敲击声开始。

definition_zh: 明亮；亮度；鲜艳程度；（声音的）明亮度；聪慧
definition_en: the quality of giving out or reflecting much light, or of being vivid, clear or quick to understand
core_image: 暗室里一盏灯被调亮，光越过桌沿，照亮整个角落
scene: 灯塔守望者在深夜调大灯芯，让一束光扫过礁石。 The lantern's brightness guided the fishing boats past the reef.
sceneCN: 这里指「光源发出的光的强弱」（第 1 个义项：发光体向四周送出光线的强度）；句意为灯塔灯的亮度引导渔船绕过暗礁。图中可辨识物件：灯芯、玻璃灯罩、扫过海面的光束、礁石。

pos.zh: 明亮；亮度；鲜明；（声音的）明亮度；聪慧

senses.title: Light given out by a source
senses.definition: the amount of light that a lamp, star or other source sends out
senses.definitionCN: 灯、恒星或其他光源发出的光的量
senses.example: The brightness of the lamp was too much for the small room.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯对这个小房间来说太亮了。
senses.why: brightness is the abstract noun of bright, so it names the quality itself rather than the thing that has it.
senses.whyCN: brightness 是 bright 的抽象名词，命名的正是「亮」这一性质，而不是发亮的物体。

senses.title: Reflected light from a surface
senses.definition: the degree to which a surface reflects light and looks light rather than dark
senses.definitionCN: 表面反射光线的程度，从而显得浅而不是深
senses.example: Fresh snow raised the brightness of the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 新雪提高了整个山谷的亮度。
senses.why: once brightness is treated as a measurable quality, it can be read off any surface, not only off lamps.
senses.whyCN: 一旦亮度被当作可测量的性质，它就能读在任何表面上，而不只属于灯。

senses.title: Vividness of a colour
senses.definition: the strength or lightness of a colour
senses.definitionCN: 颜色的强度或明度
senses.example: The restorer cleaned the canvas and the brightness of the blues returned.
senses.exampleCN: 修复师清洁了画布，蓝色的鲜艳又回来了。
senses.why: colour has its own light-like scale, so the same word moved from lamps to pigments.
senses.whyCN: 颜色本身有一套类似明暗的尺度，于是同一个词从灯移到了颜料上。

senses.title: Clearness of sound
senses.definition: the quality of a sound that is clear and high rather than dull or muffled
senses.definitionCN: 声音清晰、偏高而不沉闷含混的性质
senses.example: The new microphone added brightness to the violin's tone.
senses.exampleCN: 新麦克风让小提琴的音色更明亮。
senses.why: acoustics borrowed the visual scale: high, clean sound is called bright, and its quality is brightness.
senses.whyCN: 声学借用了视觉的尺度：高而干净的声音被称为「亮」，其性质就是 brightness。

senses.title: Apparent brightness of a star
senses.definition: the light received from a celestial body as seen from Earth
senses.definitionCN: 在地球上接收到的天体发出的光
senses.example: Astronomers recorded the brightness of the supernova every night.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家每晚记录这颗超新星的亮度。
senses.why: observers needed a word for measured light as distinct from the formal magnitude scale, and brightness filled that place.
senses.whyCN: 观测者需要一个词来指实测的光量，以区别于正式的星等标尺，brightness 正好补上这个位置。

senses.title: Screen luminance
senses.definition: the level of light set on a display or screen
senses.definitionCN: 显示器或屏幕设定的发光水平
senses.example: She lowered the brightness of her phone at night.
senses.exampleCN: 她在夜里把手机亮度调低。
senses.why: the technical sense narrowed brightness to a controllable setting on a device.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把亮度收窄为设备上一个可调节的设定值。

senses.title: Cheerful hopefulness
senses.definition: a cheerful, hopeful quality in a person or an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 人或场合中明快、充满希望的性质
senses.example: Her brightness made the long meeting feel short.
senses.exampleCN: 她的明朗让漫长的会议显得很短。
senses.why: light has long stood for happiness, so brightness carried that metaphor into mood.
senses.whyCN: 光很早就象征快乐，于是 brightness 把这层比喻带进了心情。

senses.title: Quickness of mind
senses.definition: the quality of being intelligent and quick to understand
senses.definitionCN: 聪明、理解迅速的性质
senses.example: Teachers noticed the brightness of the child in every lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们在每节课上都注意到这个孩子的聪慧。
senses.why: a bright mind is one that lights up quickly, and the noun keeps that older metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 「明亮的头脑」指很快亮起来的头脑，这个名词保留了这一较早的比喻。

intro.en: Brightness is a native English formation, built from the adjective bright and the abstract suffix -ness; its root is Germanic, so it has no Latin ancestor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: brightness 是英语本族构成，由形容词 bright 加抽象后缀 -ness 组成；其词根属日耳曼语族，没有拉丁语祖先。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English had beorhtnes, from beorht 'shining, clear' plus the abstract suffix -nes.
items.cn: 古英语已有 beorhtnes，由 beorht「发光的、清晰的」加抽象后缀 -nes 构成。

items.en: Beorht belongs to a Germanic family represented by reconstructed *berhtaz 'bright'; the reconstruction is secure as a family label but its deeper origin is not settled.
items.cn: beorht 属于以重构形式 *berhtaz「明亮的」为代表的日耳曼语族；这一重构作为语族标签较为可靠，但其更深来源没有定论。

items.en: After the Norman period the native -nes was replaced by the borrowed -ness, giving the modern shape brightness.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后，本族的 -nes 被借入的 -ness 取代，形成现代形式 brightness。

items.en: From the sixteenth century brightness was applied to colours, to sound and to the mind, each time keeping the idea of light.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，brightness 被用于颜色、声音与头脑，每次都保留「光」的观念。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became a setting on screens and a measured quantity in astronomy and acoustics.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词成为屏幕上的一个设定值，也成为天文学与声学中的可测量。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Germanic source of *berhtaz is unknown, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：*berhtaz 在日耳曼语之前的来源不明，凡为其提出的印欧词根都是重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms that are often confused with the noun; group two holds technical and near-meaning light words.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、易与这个名词混淆的形式；第二组是技术性或语义相近的光亮词。

entries.definition: The adjective that names the object which shines; brightness names the quality, so the two cannot replace each other.
entries.definitionCN: 指发亮的物体本身的形容词；brightness 命名的是性质，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: To make or become bright; it marks a change of state, while brightness is the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 使变亮或变亮；它标记状态的变化，而 brightness 是状态本身。

entries.definition: The noun of brilliant; it adds sparkle or outstanding talent, whereas brightness is the plainer measurable quality.
entries.definitionCN: brilliant 的名词；多了闪耀或出众才华的意味，而 brightness 是更朴素、可测量的性质。

entries.definition: An adverb modifying how something shines; it answers how, not what quality is present.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰发光方式的副词；回答「怎样」，而不回答「具有什么性质」。

entries.definition: A photometric term for light emitted per unit area of a surface; it is a strict measurement, while brightness is everyday and broader.
entries.definitionCN: 光度学术语，指表面单位面积发出的光；是严格的测量量，而 brightness 日常且范围更宽。

entries.definition: The total light a star emits; brightness usually means the light actually received, so the two differ in astronomy.
entries.definitionCN: 恒星发出的总光量；brightness 通常指实际接收到的光，因此在天文学中两者有别。

entries.definition: Light as it spreads outward with warmth; it is warmer and more literary than brightness.
entries.definitionCN: 光向外扩散并带暖意；比 brightness 更温暖、更文学化。

entries.definition: The act of lighting a place or the amount of light that falls on it, rather than the light a body sends out.
entries.definitionCN: 照亮某处这一动作，或落在那里的光量，而不是某物体发出的光。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词后缀、真实同族词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The suffix -ness turns the adjective bright into the abstract noun brightness.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ness 把形容词 bright 变成抽象名词 brightness。

normal.en: The family runs bright, brighten, brightly, brightening and brightness.
normal.cn: 同族形式包括 bright、brighten、brightly、brightening 与 brightness。

normal.en: Devices use brightness as a setting; astronomers use it as a measured quantity.
normal.cn: 设备把亮度当作一个设定值；天文学家把它当作可测量的量。

normal.en: Brightness is what you measure; brilliance is what you admire.
normal.cn: 亮度是量出来的；光彩是赞出来的。

normal.en: The word is Germanic, so its Latin neighbours are loanwords such as luminance and luminosity.
normal.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，因此它的拉丁近邻是 luminance、luminosity 一类的借词。

abstract.en: Picture a dimmer switch that slowly lifts a room out of darkness.
abstract.cn: 想象一个调光旋钮，把房间一点点从黑暗里提起来。

abstract.en: Picture light that left a star long ago still arriving at your eye.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗星很久以前发出的光，此刻才到达你的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a person who enters a dull room and makes it feel lighter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走进沉闷的房间，让整个房间轻快起来。

examples.en: The brightness of the screen was painful in the dark.
examples.cn: 屏幕的亮度在黑暗里刺眼。

examples.en: Astronomers compare the brightness of stars at known distances.
examples.cn: 天文学家比较已知距离上的恒星亮度。

examples.en: The brightness of her reply lifted the whole team.
examples.cn: 她回答时的明快让整个团队振作起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bright（明亮）+ -ness（性质后缀）」——亮这一性质本身 → 明亮、亮度

root: 古英语 beorht「发光的、清晰的」加抽象后缀 -nes 构成 beorhtnes；bright 属日耳曼语族，与重构形式 *berhtaz 同族，更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one quality of light: it leaves a lamp, leaves a surface, colours a pigment, clears a sound, reaches us from a star, becomes a screen setting, and finally lights a mood and a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种「光」的性质展开：它从灯发出、从表面反射、染上颜料、使声音清晰、从恒星抵达我们、变成屏幕设定，最后照亮心情与头脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp turned up in a dark room, its light reaching every corner and every surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗室里一盏灯被调亮，光到达每个角落与每个表面。

branches.en: MEASURED LIGHT: what a lamp or a star sends out can be compared on one scale.
branches.cn: 可量的光：灯或恒星送出的光可以放在同一把尺上比较。

branches.en: SURFACE AND PIGMENT: the quality is read off what reflects it, not only off what emits it.
branches.cn: 表面与颜料：这一性质可以从反射它的东西上读出，而不只从发光体上读出。

branches.en: CLEAR SOUND: acoustics borrows the visual scale and calls clean, high sound bright.
branches.cn: 清亮的声音：声学借用视觉尺度，把干净偏高的声音称作「亮」。

branches.en: DEVICE SETTING: a physical quantity becomes a knob the user can turn.
branches.cn: 设备设定：一个物理量变成了用户可以拧动的旋钮。

branches.en: MOOD AND MIND: light stands for cheerfulness and for quick understanding.
branches.cn: 心情与头脑：光象征明朗快乐，也象征理解迅速。

intro.en: Brightness is transparently built from an adjective plus a productive noun suffix, so its morphology can be read without guesswork.
intro.cn: brightness 由一个形容词加一个能产的名词后缀透明地构成，因此其形态可以不经猜测直接读出。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so it has no Latin entries; the Latin layer of English supplies the technical neighbours luminance and luminosity instead.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，因此没有拉丁条目；英语的拉丁层改为提供 luminance 与 luminosity 这类技术近邻。

items.example: A bright star stood over the bay.
items.exampleCN: 一颗明亮的星悬在海湾上方。

items.meaning: the state or quality of being
items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a name for its quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成其性质的名词。

items.example: The brightness of the lamp filled the room.

items.meaning: the act or process of becoming bright
items.example: The sky showed a slow brightening.
The overbright sign washed out the street.
items.exampleCN: 过亮的招牌把街景照得发白。

items.example: The bright-eyed child ran to the door.
items.exampleCN: 那个眼睛明亮的孩子跑向门口。

items.meaning: a graded set of brightness levels
items.example: The chart shows a brightness scale from one to ten.
items.exampleCN: 图表给出从一到十的亮度等级。

definition_zh: v. 使（货币）贬值；贬低；轻视（使显得不重要）
definition_en: to reduce the official exchange value of a currency, or to make something or someone seem less important
core_image: 汇率牌上数字一夜之间往下跳；一个人把别人的建议随手推到桌角
scene: 政府让货币贬值了。 The government devalued the currency.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：devalued 指使贬值；句意是政府让货币贬值了。

senses.title: Lower a currency worth
senses.definition: to reduce the official exchange value of a currency
senses.definitionCN: 降低一种货币的官方兑换价值
senses.example: The government devalued the currency.
senses.exampleCN: 政府让货币贬值了。
senses.why: A rate board with the figure shifted down overnight.
senses.whyCN: 一块汇率牌，数字一夜之间被调低。

senses.title: Make something seem less worth
senses.definition: to make something appear less important or valuable
senses.definitionCN: 使某物显得不那么重要或有价值
senses.example: The comment devalued her research.
senses.exampleCN: 那条评论贬低了她的研究。
senses.why: A report pushed to the corner of a desk.
senses.whyCN: 一份被推到桌角的报告。

senses.title: Treat a person as less worth
senses.definition: to make a person feel that they are not valued
senses.definitionCN: 让一个人觉得自己不被重视
senses.example: He felt devalued by the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定让他觉得自己不被重视。
senses.why: A name badge left off a staff list.
senses.whyCN: 员工名单上被漏掉的一个姓名牌。

intro.en: Devalue is de- down plus value, from Old French valoir, from Latin valere, to be strong or worth.
intro.cn: devalue 由 de-（向下）加 value 构成；value 来自古法语 valoir，源自拉丁语 valere（强健、有价值）。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong or worth.
items.cn: valere 意为强健、有价值。

items.en: Valoir meant to be worth.
items.cn: 古法语 valoir 意为值得。

items.en: Value entered English for worth.
items.cn: 十五世纪 value 以价值义进入英语。

items.en: Devalue appeared for lowering value.
items.cn: 十九世纪 devalue 出现，表示降低价值。

items.en: Devaluation became a standard policy term.
items.cn: 二十世纪 devaluation 成为标准政策术语。

items.en: It now also covers belittling people.
items.cn: 如今它也用于描述贬低人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the val- worth family; the near-meaning group names other ways of lowering worth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 val-（价值）家族；近义组是其他表示「降低价值」的词。

entries.definition: Worth, or to regard as important; devalue adds de- to push it down.
entries.definitionCN: 价值，或重视；devalue 加 de- 把它往下压。

entries.definition: To judge the worth of something; it shares valere but measures rather than lowers.
entries.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值；共享 valere，但是衡量而非降低。

entries.definition: The act of lowering a currency value.
entries.definitionCN: 降低币值的行为。

entries.definition: To lose value over time, especially by market forces.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间失去价值，尤指受市场力量影响。

entries.definition: To make someone or something seem unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物显得不重要。

entries.definition: To move something to a lower level or rating.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物降到更低的级别或评级。

normalIntro.en: Devalue is de- down plus val- worth: move the worth down, on a board or in a mind.
normalIntro.cn: devalue 就是 de-（向下）加 val-（价值）：把价值往下移，无论是在牌子上还是在人心里。

normal.en: Val- means worth, as in value.
normal.cn: val- 意为价值，如 value。

normal.en: Devalue is deliberate; depreciate is often natural.
normal.cn: devalue 是人为的，depreciate 常是自然发生的。

normal.en: Devaluation is the noun for a currency.
normal.cn: devaluation 是用于货币的名词。

normal.en: Devalue their work means belittle it.
normal.cn: devalue their work 就是贬低他们的成果。

normal.en: Feel devalued means feel unimportant.
normal.cn: feel devalued 就是觉得自己不重要。

abstract.en: A rate board with the figure shifted down overnight.
abstract.cn: 一块汇率牌，数字一夜之间被调低。

abstract.en: A report pushed to the corner of a desk.
abstract.cn: 一份被推到桌角的报告。

abstract.en: A name badge left off a staff list.
abstract.cn: 员工名单上被漏掉的一个姓名牌。

examples.en: They devalued the pound by ten percent.
examples.cn: 他们让英镑贬值百分之十。

examples.en: Such remarks devalue the whole team.
examples.cn: 这类言论贬低了整个团队。

examples.en: The award was devalued by too many winners.
examples.cn: 获奖者太多，这个奖也就贬值了。

dict_mnemonic.text: devalue ＝ de（向下）＋ value（价值，拉丁语 valere「强健、值得」，与 valid、valuable 同根）＝把价值往下压，「使贬值、贬低」。

root: 拉丁语 valere（强健、有价值）→ 古法语 valoir → value（价值）→ de-＋value → devalue

sensesIntro.en: One figure moved down: a rate board, a pushed report and a missing name.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个被调低的数字：一块汇率牌、一份被推开的报告与一个被漏掉的名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rate board with the figure shifted down overnight
core.cn: 核心意象：一块汇率牌，数字一夜之间被调低

branches.en: A rate board with the figure shifted down overnight.
branches.cn: 一块汇率牌，数字一夜之间被调低。

branches.en: A report pushed to the corner of a desk.
branches.cn: 一份被推到桌角的报告。

branches.en: A name badge left off a staff list.
branches.cn: 员工名单上被漏掉的一个姓名牌。

branches.en: Both lower a stated worth.
branches.cn: 两者都降低一个被标出的价值。

branches.en: Both make a person feel smaller.
branches.cn: 两者都让人觉得自己变小了。

intro.en: Devalue is de- plus val-; the worth root also builds value, valid and evaluate.
intro.cn: devalue 由 de- 加 val- 构成；价值这个词根也造出 value、valid 与 evaluate。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere means to be strong, pretium a price and gradus a step.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为强健，pretium 意为价格，gradus 意为台阶。

definition_zh: 反传统者；抨击偶像者；破坏圣像者
definition_en: a person who attacks established beliefs, images or customs
core_image: 一个人站在挂满画像的墙前，伸手把最中央那幅取下来，放到地上
scene: 所有人都在称赞那套流程，只有他站起来问了一句最基础的问题。 The iconoclast was invited back every year.
sceneCN: 这里 iconoclast 指挑战既有信条的人（第 2 个义项：抨击信条者）；句意为这位反传统者每年都被请回来。

pos.zh: 反传统者；抨击偶像者；破坏圣像者

collocations.zh: 无所畏惧的偶像破坏者

senses.title: Breaker of images
senses.definition: a person who destroys religious images as idolatrous
senses.definitionCN: 以偶像崇拜为由毁坏宗教圣像的人
senses.example: In the eighth century the iconoclast removed every painted face from the church.
senses.exampleCN: 八世纪时，破坏圣像者把教堂里每一张绘出的面容都取了下来。
senses.why: This is the historical sense: the word was born in a war over whether images may be worshipped.
senses.whyCN: 这是历史义：这个词诞生于一场关于图像能否被崇拜的战争。

senses.title: Attacker of beliefs
senses.definition: a person who challenges accepted doctrines held as sacred
senses.definitionCN: 挑战被视为神圣的既定信条的人
senses.example: The iconoclast was invited back every year.
senses.exampleCN: 这位反传统者每年都被请回来。
senses.why: Once images became ideas, breaking them became argument rather than demolition.
senses.whyCN: 当图像变成观念，破坏它就从拆毁变成了论证。

senses.title: Challenger of tradition
senses.definition: someone who questions customs simply because they are old
senses.definitionCN: 仅仅因为习俗古老就加以质疑的人
senses.example: Every tradition needs at least one iconoclast to stay honest.
senses.exampleCN: 每种传统都至少需要一个反传统者来保持诚实。
senses.why: Age alone is not an argument, and the challenger is right to say so once.
senses.whyCN: 年岁本身不是论据，挑战者说一次这话是对的。

senses.title: Reformer in an institution
senses.definition: a member who attacks the habits of their own organisation
senses.definitionCN: 攻击自己组织习惯的成员
senses.example: As an iconoclast inside the bank, she abolished three rituals.
senses.exampleCN: 作为银行里的破规者，她废掉了三项仪式。
senses.why: Reform from inside is slower and more effective, because the critic knows which wall bears weight.
senses.whyCN: 内部改革更慢也更有效，因为批评者知道哪堵墙承重。

senses.title: Critic of heroes
senses.definition: a person who refuses to treat admired figures as flawless
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝把受敬仰者当作无瑕之人的人
senses.example: The biography was written by an iconoclast who loved its subject.
senses.exampleCN: 这本传记出自一位爱传主的反偶像者。
senses.why: A hero treated as flawless stops being a model and becomes a fence.
senses.whyCN: 被当作无瑕的英雄不再是榜样，而成了一道围栏。

senses.title: Artistic rule-breaker
senses.definition: an artist who abandons the accepted forms of the day
senses.definitionCN: 抛弃当时通行形式的艺术家
senses.example: The iconoclast hung the painting upside down and changed the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这位破规者把画倒挂，改变了整个房间。
senses.why: Forms are tools; when a tool hides the thing it should show, breaking it is reasonable.
senses.whyCN: 形式是工具；当工具遮住了它该显示的东西，打破它就是合理的。

senses.title: The needed voice
senses.definition: the dissent that keeps a group from repeating its mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 使团体不再重复错误的异议
senses.example: They kept one iconoclast on every committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在每个委员会里都留一位异声。
senses.why: A group without dissent cannot tell the difference between agreement and silence.
senses.whyCN: 没有异议的团体分不清同意与沉默。

senses.title: Iconoclasm as habit
senses.definition: a standing habit of attacking whatever is respected
senses.definitionCN: 攻击一切受敬之物的固定习气
senses.example: His iconoclasm had become a reflex, not a position.
senses.exampleCN: 他的反偶像已成条件反射，而不是立场。
senses.why: The same impulse that clears dead forms can also break what is still alive.
senses.whyCN: 清除死形式的同一冲动，也会打破仍然活着的东西。

intro.en: Iconoclast joins two Greek words, image and breaker, and its history begins in a church dispute over pictures.
intro.cn: iconoclast 把两个希腊词「图像」与「破坏者」接在一起，历史始于教会关于图像的争论。

items.en: Eikon meant 'image, likeness', especially a painted holy figure.
items.cn: eikon 意为「图像、相似物」，尤指绘制的圣像。

items.en: Klastes meant 'breaker', from klan 'to break', the source of clastic.
items.cn: klastes 意为「破坏者」，出自 klan「打破」，是 clastic 的来源。

items.en: Iconoclasts destroyed images in the 8c. on the grounds that worship of them was idolatry.
items.cn: 八世纪的破坏圣像者以崇拜图像属偶像崇拜为由毁坏图像。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the 16c., first for the historical party.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个词，最初指那个历史派别。

items.en: By the 19c. any attacker of accepted beliefs could be called an iconoclast.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，任何攻击既定信念的人都能被称为 iconoclast。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the image-breaking pieces; the near-meaning group names kinds of challengers.
note.cn: 形近组共享「破像」的部件；近义组列出不同种类的挑战者。

entries.definition: the attacking of images or beliefs.
entries.definitionCN: 对图像或信念的攻击。

entries.definition: breaking accepted images or rules.
entries.definitionCN: 打破既定形象或规则的。

entries.definition: the study or system of images.
entries.definitionCN: 图像的研究或体系。

entries.definition: a venerated image or symbol.
entries.definitionCN: 受敬奉的图像或象征。

entries.definition: a person who fights against established power.
entries.definitionCN: 与既定权力斗争的人。

entries.definition: one who disagrees with an official view.
entries.definitionCN: 不赞同官方看法的人。

entries.definition: a person who wants deep change of the system.
entries.definitionCN: 主张制度深层改变的人。

entries.definition: one who holds a belief condemned as false.
entries.definitionCN: 持被斥为虚假信念的人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a painting being taken down from the centre of the wall.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一幅画被人从墙的正中央取下来」的画面。

normal.en: Iconoclast = icon + clast: an image breaker, exactly as spelled.
normal.cn: iconoclast = icon + clast：破坏图像的人，正是字面意思。

normal.en: Clast also hides in clastic rock: broken pieces pressed together.
normal.cn: clast 也藏在 clastic rock（碎屑岩）里：碎块被压在一起。

normal.en: Think of someone asking the question everyone has agreed not to ask.
normal.cn: 想象有人问出大家都默契地不问的那个问题。

normal.en: Say eye-KON-uh-klast; the eye at the start sounds like an eye looking at an image.
normal.cn: 读成 eye-KON-uh-klast，开头的 eye 像一只眼睛在看图像。

normal.en: Link with icon: every iconoclast needs an icon first.
normal.cn: 和 icon 联系：每个反偶像者都得先有一个偶像。

abstract.en: Breaking an image is easy; replacing the need for it is the real work.
abstract.cn: 打破图像容易；替代对它的需要才是真正的工作。

abstract.en: A healthy tradition keeps one person who is allowed to be rude to it.
abstract.cn: 健康的传统会留一个被允许对它无礼的人。

abstract.en: The habit of attack can clear dead wood or cut living branches.
abstract.cn: 攻击的习气既能清掉枯枝，也能砍断活枝。

examples.en: The iconoclast was invited back every year.
examples.cn: 这位反传统者每年都被请回来。

examples.en: Every tradition needs at least one iconoclast to stay honest.
examples.cn: 每种传统都至少需要一个反传统者来保持诚实。

examples.en: As an iconoclast inside the bank, she abolished three rituals.
examples.cn: 作为银行里的破规者，她废掉了三项仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: icon（圣像）+ clast（打破的人）：打破圣像的人，就是「反传统者」。

root: 希腊语 eikon（图像）+ klastes（破坏者）

sensesIntro.en: An iconoclast breaks something treated as untouchable; the senses differ in whether the target is an image, a doctrine, a custom or a hero.
sensesIntro.cn: iconoclast 打碎被当作不可触碰之物；各义项的差别在于对象是图像、教义、习俗，还是英雄。

core.en: BREAKING WHAT IS TREATED AS UNTOUCHABLE
core.cn: 打碎不可触碰之物

branches.en: The historical breaking of religious images.
branches.cn: 历史上对宗教图像的破坏。

branches.en: Doctrines and customs attacked by argument.
branches.cn: 以论证攻击的教义与习俗。

branches.en: The internal reformer and the useful dissenting voice.
branches.cn: 内部改革者与有用的异声。

branches.en: Heroes questioned and forms abandoned.
branches.cn: 被质疑的英雄与被抛弃的形式。

branches.en: The habit of attack, which can outlive its purpose.
branches.cn: 攻击的习气，可能活得比它的目的更久。

intro.en: The icon family is about images and their authority: an icon is honoured, iconography studies them, iconoclasm breaks them.
intro.cn: icon 词族与图像及其权威有关：icon 受敬奉，iconography 研究它们，iconoclasm 打破它们。

latinIntro.en: Greek eikon and klastes are the two halves; the first gives the target, the second the act, and the compound is a small programme.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 eikon 与 klastes 是两半：前者给对象，后者给动作，这个复合词本身就是一个小纲领。

definition_zh: 全球市场；世界市场；某一产品的全球需求与交易体系
definition_en: the worldwide system in which goods, services and capital are bought and sold across national borders
core_image: 一颗地球仪上密布着连线，每一条线两端各是一处港口或交易所，货物与资金沿线来回
scene: 跨国公司的会议室里，墙上挂着一幅世界地图，负责人指着几处港口说，产品要在所有国家同时销售。 The directors studied how the product would compete in the global market.
sceneCN: 这里指「全球范围的市场体系」，对应第 1 个义项：跨越各国边界的买卖与竞争场所；句意为董事们研究该产品将如何在全球市场中竞争。画面要点：世界地图、港口标记、会议桌、销售图表。

pos.zh: 全球市场；世界市场（可数，常用单数指整体体系，复数指多个区域市场）

collocations.phrase: a player in the global market

全球化（globalize 加名词后缀，指跨国整合的过程）

市场场所（market 加 place 构成的复合词，指交易发生的具体场所）
营销（market 加动名词后缀，语义从「市场」转为「开拓市场的行为」）

senses.title: The worldwide trading arena
senses.definition: the worldwide system in which goods, services and capital are exchanged across borders
senses.definitionCN: 货物、服务与资本跨国交换的世界性体系
senses.example: The directors studied how the product would compete in the global market.
senses.exampleCN: 董事们研究该产品将如何在全球市场上竞争。
senses.why: Global extends Latin globus 'sphere' to the whole earth, and market names a place of trade, so the phrase is the trading place of the whole sphere.
senses.whyCN: global 把拉丁 globus「球体」扩展到整个地球，market 指交易之所，合起来就是整个球面上的交易场所。

senses.title: Combined demand from all countries
senses.titleCN: 所有国家买方的合计需求
senses.definition: the total demand for a category of goods from buyers in every country
senses.definitionCN: 各国买方对某一类货物的需求总和
senses.example: Demand for the device grew across the global market.
senses.exampleCN: 全球市场对该设备的需求增长了。
senses.why: A market can mean the buyers themselves, so a global market is the sum of buyers everywhere rather than a physical place.
senses.whyCN: 市场也可以指买方本身，因此全球市场就是各地买方的总和，而不是一个实体场所。

senses.title: The worldwide market for one product
senses.definition: the worldwide supply and demand for a single product or service
senses.definitionCN: 单一产品或服务在世界范围内的供给与需求
senses.example: The global market for memory chips is highly concentrated.
senses.exampleCN: 存储芯片的全球市场高度集中。
senses.why: Naming the product narrows the sphere to one trade, as in the steel market or the car market.
senses.whyCN: 点明产品就把整个球面收窄到一桩生意，如钢铁市场或汽车市场。

senses.title: The international capital market
senses.definition: the cross-border system in which money, securities and credit are traded
senses.definitionCN: 资金、证券与信贷跨境交易的世界性体系
senses.example: Pension funds move capital through the global market every day.
senses.exampleCN: 养老基金每天都在全球市场中调度资本。
senses.why: Finance uses the same arena image, but the cargo is money and the ports are exchanges.
senses.whyCN: 金融沿用同一个场所意象，只是货物变成金钱，港口变成交易所。

senses.title: Access to customers outside one's country
senses.titleCN: 进入本国之外客户群的通道
senses.definition: the opportunity for a firm to sell to customers in other countries
senses.definitionCN: 企业向他国客户销售的机会
senses.example: Small firms struggle to reach the global market without partners.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业若没有伙伴，很难进入全球市场。
senses.why: From a company's viewpoint the phrase names an opening rather than a place, and entry becomes the key verb.
senses.whyCN: 从企业视角看，这个短语指一扇打开的门而不是一个地点，因此「进入」成了常用动词。

senses.title: Worldwide competitive position
senses.definition: the rank or share that a firm holds in worldwide sales of a product
senses.definitionCN: 企业在某产品的世界销售额中所占的排名或份额
senses.example: The company holds a third of the global market in turbines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司占全球涡轮机市场的三分之一。
senses.why: Share language turns the arena into a pie to be divided, so the phrase measures position rather than describes trade.
senses.whyCN: 份额的说法把竞技场变成一块待分的饼，于是这个短语衡量的是地位，而不是描述贸易。

senses.title: The price level set worldwide
senses.titleCN: 由全球供求形成的价格水平
senses.definition: the price of a commodity determined by worldwide supply and demand rather than local conditions
senses.definitionCN: 由世界范围供求而非本地情况决定的商品价格
senses.example: Wheat prices now follow the global market, not the village harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦价格如今跟着全球市场走，而不是看村里收成。
senses.why: When buyers and sellers are everywhere, no single locality sets the price, so the phrase denotes a price formed collectively.
senses.whyCN: 当买卖双方遍布各地，任何单一场地都无法定价，因此这个短语指集体形成的价格。

senses.title: Worldwide competition as an arena
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把全球竞争视作一个竞技场
senses.definition: the abstract arena in which firms, cities or ideas compete for worldwide attention and sales
senses.definitionCN: 企业、城市或观念争夺全球关注与销售份额的抽象竞技场
senses.example: Universities now compete in a global market for students.
senses.exampleCN: 大学如今在学生这一全球市场中相互竞争。
senses.why: The metaphor widens once more: anything that can attract people or money can be said to have a global market.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻再度扩展：凡能吸引人或钱的东西，都可以说拥有一个全球市场。

intro.en: Global market joins two separate Latin lines: global from globus 'sphere', market from mercatus 'trade'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: global market 联结了两条独立的拉丁语线索：global 出自 globus「球体」，market 出自 mercatus「交易」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Globus meant a ball or sphere, and it was used for the round earth by Roman writers.
items.cn: globus 意为球或球体，罗马作家也用它指圆形的大地。

items.en: French formed global in the sense of taking the whole into one view, and English adopted it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语构成 global，意为把整体纳入一个视野；英语在 17 世纪吸收了它。

items.en: Mercatus meant trade or a marketplace, from mercari 'to trade' and merx 'merchandise'.
items.cn: mercatus 意为交易或市场，出自 mercari「做买卖」与 merx「货物」。

items.en: Old English borrowed market through Latin and French, first as a place and then as the demand found there.
items.cn: 古英语经拉丁语与法语借入 market，最初指地点，随后指那里出现的需求。

items.en: Global market became common in the late twentieth century as transport and finance knit national markets together.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，随着运输与金融把各国市场织在一起，global market 成为常用说法。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two roots and looks close; the second group names markets that differ by scope.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个词根之一且外形相近；第二组是按范围区分的不同市场。

entries.definition: A sphere or a model of the earth; it is the object from which the adjective global was made, not a trading place.
entries.definitionCN: 球体或地球模型；它是 global 这个形容词的来源物，不是交易场所。

entries.definition: The process of knitting economies and cultures together; a global market is one result of that process, not the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 把经济与文化织在一起的过程；全球市场是该过程的一个结果，而不是过程本身。

entries.definition: A concrete place or platform where buying and selling happen; global market stresses scope rather than location.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖发生的具体地点或平台；global market 强调的是范围而不是位置。

entries.definition: A trading place, shortened from market but influenced by Dutch; it names a local venue, not a worldwide system.
entries.definitionCN: 交易场所，由 market 缩略并受荷兰语影响；它指本地场地，而非世界体系。

entries.definition: Nearly interchangeable with global market; world is native English and global is the Latin-derived formal variant.
entries.definitionCN: 与 global market 几乎可互换；world 是英语本族词，global 是拉丁来源的正式变体。

entries.definition: Trade between countries; it stresses relations across borders, while global market stresses the whole as one arena.
entries.definitionCN: 国家之间的贸易；它强调跨国关系，而 global market 强调整体是一个竞技场。

entries.definition: Markets beyond the sea from the speaker's country; the phrase is relative to a home base, unlike global market.
entries.definitionCN: 从说话者本国看去的海外市场；这个说法相对于本国而言，而 global market 不带立场。

entries.definition: A group of countries treating their economies as one market, such as a customs union; it is regional, not worldwide.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干国家经济体当作一个市场的集团，如关税同盟；它是区域性的，不是全球的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the sphere root, the trade root and real market phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：球体词根、交易词根与真实市场搭配。

normal.en: Global is the whole sphere; market is where trade happens; the phrase is trade on the whole sphere.
normal.cn: global 是整个球面，market 是交易发生之处，短语就是整个球面上的交易。

normal.en: The two halves come from different Latin words: globus for the sphere, mercatus for trade.
normal.cn: 两半来自不同的拉丁词：globus 指球体，mercatus 指交易。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: global market share, global market prices, enter the global market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：全球市场份额、全球市场价格、进入全球市场。

normal.en: Global market is uncountable in its system sense and countable when it means several regional markets.
normal.cn: 指整个体系时不可数，指多个区域市场时可数。

normal.en: The phrase is about scope, so it pairs with verbs of reaching and competing, not with verbs of visiting.
normal.cn: 这个短语讲范围，因此常与「抵达」「竞争」类动词搭配，而不与「到访」类动词搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a globe wrapped in threads, each thread a trade route with a price tag at both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗地球仪被线缠满，每根线是一条商路，两端各挂一个价签。

abstract.en: Picture one enormous auction hall with every country's flag on the wall and one running price board.
abstract.cn: 想象一座巨大的拍卖厅，墙上挂着各国旗帜，只有一块跳动的价目板。

abstract.en: Picture a stadium whose seats are filled by buyers from every continent, all watching the same scoreboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一座体育场，座位上坐满各洲来的买方，共同盯着同一块记分牌。

examples.en: The firm sells to the global market rather than to one region.
examples.cn: 这家公司面向全球市场销售，而不是只做一个区域。

examples.en: Cheap freight opened the global market to small producers.
examples.cn: 低廉的运费向小生产者打开了全球市场。

examples.en: Its global market share slipped as rivals expanded.
examples.cn: 随着对手扩张，它的全球市场份额下滑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「整个地球的集市」——球面全算进来，货物在各国之间买卖 → 全球市场

root: global 出自拉丁 globus「球体」，经法语 global 进入英语；market 出自拉丁 mercatus「交易」，源 merx「货物」。两者合成「覆盖整个地球的交易场」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same arena at different scales: the whole system, its combined demand, one product's worldwide trade, capital flows, a firm's access, its share, a world price and finally any competition for worldwide attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一竞技场的不同尺度：整个体系、其合计需求、单一产品的世界贸易、资本流动、企业的进入通道、企业份额、世界价格，最后是任何争夺全球关注的竞争。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a globe threaded with trade routes, each ending in a price.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗缠满商路的地球仪，每条路的尽头都标着价格。

branches.en: BASE ARENA: the trading place of the whole sphere.
branches.cn: 基础竞技场：整个球面的交易场所。

branches.en: DEMAND AND PRODUCT: the arena can be summed as buyers, or narrowed to one trade.
branches.cn: 需求与产品：这个竞技场可汇成买方总和，也可收窄到一桩生意。

branches.en: CAPITAL: the cargo becomes money and the ports become exchanges.
branches.cn: 资本：货物变成金钱，港口变成交易所。

branches.en: FIRM VIEW: the arena is an opening to be entered and a share to be held.
branches.cn: 企业视角：竞技场是一扇可进入的门，也是一份可持有的份额。

branches.en: PRICE AND METAPHOR: a world price forms, and any contest can be called a global market.
branches.cn: 价格与比喻：世界价格形成，任何争夺都可被称为全球市场。

intro.en: Global market is a phrase of two free words, each with a Latin root and a productive family.
intro.cn: global market 是由两个自由词构成的短语，各自有拉丁词根与能产的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin globus 'sphere' gives globe, global, globalization; Latin mercatus 'trade' gives market, marketing, marketplace and merchant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 globus「球体」衍生 globe、global、globalization；拉丁 mercatus「交易」衍生 market、marketing、marketplace 与 merchant。

items.exampleCN: 这个成分构成一批关于圆形与整体的词。

items.exampleCN: 他们在全球市场上竞争。

definition_zh: 古物收藏家；古旧文物的；爱好古物的
definition_en: a person who studies or collects old and rare things, or relating to the study of antiquities
core_image: 一屋子旧书与铜器，主人用白手套轻抚书脊
scene: 旧书店深处，煤油灯下的书堆泛着黄。 The antiquarian spent his weekends hunting for maps of the old harbor.
sceneCN: 这里 antiquarian 是「古物收藏家」（第 1 个义项：搜集研究古物之人）；句意为这位古物爱好者周末都在寻找旧港湾地图。

pos.zh: 古物收藏家；文物研究者

derivatives.zh: 同族词，义为「古物研究者」，更古雅的说法
由本词加 -ism 构成，义为「古物癖；好古之风」

senses.title: A collector or student of antiquities
senses.titleCN: 古物收藏家；文物研究者
senses.definition: a person who collects, studies, or deals in old books, maps, coins, and other relics of the past
senses.definitionCN: 收集、研究或经营旧书、古地图、古币等旧物的人
senses.example: The antiquarian could date a coin by the wear on its edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古物收藏家凭边缘的磨损就能断定古币的年代。
senses.why: Latin antiquus 'old' plus the agent ending -arian names the person devoted to old things.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 antiquus「古老的」加表人后缀 -arian，点出倾心旧物之人。

senses.title: Relating to old and rare things
senses.definition: connected with the collecting or study of antiquities, or old-fashioned in flavor
senses.definitionCN: 与古物收藏研究相关，或带有古旧风味的
senses.example: The library keeps its antiquarian maps in a dark, cool room.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆把古籍地图存放在阴凉的暗室。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the noun's devotion: anything flavored with age can be antiquarian.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了名词的痴迷：凡带着岁月风味的东西皆可称 antiquarian。

intro.en: Antiquarian is antiquary reshaped: Latin antiquus 'old' plus the person-ending -arian.
intro.cn: antiquarian 由 antiquary 变形而来：拉丁语 antiquus「古老的」加表人后缀 -arian。

items.en: The root *ant- meant 'front, before', the same root that feeds ante- and ancient.
items.cn: 词根 *ant- 意为「前面、在先」，同样滋养 ante- 与 ancient。

items.en: Antiquus meant 'old, former', source of antique and antiquity.
items.cn: antiquus 意为「古老的、从前的」，是 antique 与 antiquity 的来源。

items.en: Late Latin had antiquarius, a keeper or maker of old things.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语已有 antiquarius，指旧物的守护者或制作者。

items.en: English had antiquary first, then built the longer antiquarian in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语先有 antiquary，十七世纪又构成更长的 antiquarian。

items.en: Today the word lives mostly in bookshops, auctions, and scholarly societies.
items.cn: 如今该词主要活跃于旧书店、拍卖行与学术团体。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the antiquus family and look-alike -arian words; the near-meaning group gathers old-things words.
note.cn: 形近组收 antiquus 词族与易混 -arian 词；近义组收「旧物」类词。

entries.definition: Ancient times, or a very old object.
entries.definitionCN: 古代；古老之物。

entries.definition: An old collectible object, or very old in style.
entries.definitionCN: 古董；古式的。

entries.definition: Relating to land and farming; shares the -arian ending only.
entries.definitionCN: 土地与农业的；仅共享 -arian 词尾。

entries.definition: Anyone who gathers things of a kind.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指各类收藏者。

entries.definition: A keeper of records and documents.
entries.definitionCN: 档案与文书的保管者。

entries.definition: A keeper of a museum's collections.
entries.definitionCN: 博物馆藏品的策展守护人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the antiquus 'old' root and the -arian person ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 antiquus「古老」词根与 -arian 表人词尾。

normal.en: antiqu + arian: a person devoted to old things.
normal.cn: antiqu 加 arian：倾心旧物的人。

normal.en: Antique and antiquity share the same old root.
normal.cn: antique 与 antiquity 同根。

normal.en: An antiquarian bookshop sells old, rare books.
normal.cn: antiquarian bookshop 卖古籍珍本。

normal.en: The older word is antiquary, one letter shorter.
normal.cn: 更旧的词是 antiquary，少一个字母。

normal.en: -arian also gives librarian and vegetarian: person endings.
normal.cn: -arian 还见于 librarian、vegetarian：都是表人词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass hovering over a faded signature.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜悬在褪色的签名上方。

abstract.en: Picture shelves of leather spines smelling of dust and time.
abstract.cn: 想象一排皮革书脊，散发尘土与岁月的气味。

abstract.en: Picture white gloves turning the pages of a cracked map.
abstract.cn: 想象白手套翻动脆裂的古地图。

examples.en: The antiquarian paid a fortune for the first edition.
examples.cn: 这位古物爱好者花巨资买下初版书。

examples.en: Her antiquarian interests began with grandmother's coins.
examples.cn: 她的好古之趣始于祖母的旧硬币。

examples.en: The sale featured antiquarian prints of the city.
examples.cn: 拍卖会推出了这座城市的古版画。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安提葵」——安安静静对着古葵（老物件）研究的人，就是「古物收藏家」

root: 拉丁语 antiquus（古老的）+ -arius（从事者）→ 拉丁 antiquarius → 英语 antiquarian；核心意象是「以旧物为业与乐的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The devoted person and the adjective describing their world share one love of age.
sensesIntro.cn: 痴迷的人与形容其天地的形容词共享同一种对岁月的爱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands in white gloves reaching into the dust of time
core.cn: 核心意象：戴着白手套的手伸进时间的尘埃

branches.en: The person line: the hunter of books, coins, and maps.
branches.cn: 人物线：追逐古籍、古币与古地图的猎人。

branches.en: The thing line: shops, prints, and societies with the same name.
branches.cn: 物象线：同名书店、版画与学会。

branches.en: Both honor the past by keeping its leftovers whole.
branches.cn: 两者都通过完整保存遗存来致敬过去。

branches.en: The flavor line: antiquarian can mean pleasantly old-fashioned.
branches.cn: 风味线：antiquarian 也可指令人愉悦的古雅。

branches.en: The scholarship line: antiquarians were historians' amateur ancestors.
branches.cn: 学术线：古物研究者是历史学家的业余先祖。

intro.en: The word is the antiqu- 'old' root plus the -arian person ending, a Latin doublet.
intro.cn: 这个词是 antiqu-「古老」词根加 -arian 表人词尾的拉丁组合。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entry shows antiquarius, the late-Latin keeper of old things.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示 antiquarius，即晚期拉丁语的旧物守护者。

items.example: It forms antemeridian, from the same ancient root.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 antemeridian，出自同一古老词根。

items.example: It shares the *ant- front root through Old French.
items.exampleCN: 它经古法语共享 *ant- 词根。

items.example: It is the shorter, older form of antiquarian.
items.exampleCN: 它是 antiquarian 更短更旧的形式。

items.example: Librarian shares the -arian ending with antiquarian.
items.exampleCN: librarian 与 antiquarian 共享 -arian 词尾。

latinEntries.meaning: a keeper or dealer in old things
latinEntries.meaningCN: 旧物的守护者或经营者

definition_zh: 微生物的；由微生物引起的；与微生物有关的
definition_en: of, relating to, or caused by microbes
core_image: 岩石表面一层黏滑的绿色菌席，在放大镜下由无数微小细胞连成一片
scene: 这里指「微生物的」。 The microbial mat on the rock surface turned the shallow water green.
sceneCN: 这里 microbial 是「微生物的」（第 1 个义项：与微生物相关）；句意：岩石表面的微生物席把浅水染成了绿色。图中可辨识物件：岩石、贴附其上的菌席、被映绿的水面。

pos.zh: 微生物的；由微生物引起的（由名词 microbe 加 -ial 构成，范围比 bacterial 更宽）

derivatives.zh: 微生物（尤指致病的微小生物）
微生物区系；特定生境的微生物群落

senses.title: Of Microbes in General
senses.titleCN: 微生物的：与微生物这一类相关
senses.definition: relating to microbes as a broad class of small life
senses.definitionCN: 与作为一大类微小生命的微生物有关的
senses.example: Microbial life exists in every handful of garden soil.
senses.exampleCN: 每一把园土里都有微生物生命。
senses.why: Microbial is built on microbe, a popular nineteenth-century word for small life. The suffix -ial marks relation, so the adjective is wider than bacterial and can cover fungi and protists as well.
senses.whyCN: microbial 建立在 microbe 上，那是十九世纪指微小生命的通俗词；后缀 -ial 表示关联，因此这个形容词比 bacterial 更宽，也能涵盖真菌与原生生物。

senses.title: Microbial Life
senses.titleCN: 微生物生命：作为生命形态本身
senses.definition: the living activity of microbes taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把微生物作为整体来看的生命活动
senses.example: Microbial life in the vent thrives without sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 热泉喷口处的微生物生命不依赖阳光而繁盛。
senses.why: Here the adjective modifies life itself, not a process or a disease. The phrase treats microbes as a form of life with its own chemistry, such as chemosynthesis.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词修饰的是「生命」本身，而不是某个过程或疾病；该短语把微生物视为一种有自身化学机制（如化能合成）的生命形态。

senses.title: A Microbial Community
senses.titleCN: 微生物群落的：共同生活的集合
senses.definition: relating to a community or assemblage of microbes
senses.definitionCN: 与微生物群落或集合体有关的
senses.example: The microbial community in the gut shifted after the antibiotic.
senses.exampleCN: 使用抗生素后，肠道中的微生物群落发生了变化。
senses.why: A community is more than many cells; it is a set of populations that interact. The adjective marks that ecological level, which is why microbial community and microbiome are so frequent.
senses.whyCN: 群落不只是许多细胞，而是相互作用的种群集合；这个形容词标出的是生态层次，因此 microbial community 与 microbiome 如此常用。

senses.title: Microbial Growth
senses.titleCN: 微生物生长的：数量增加的过程
senses.definition: relating to the increase of microbial populations
senses.definitionCN: 与微生物种群数量增加有关的
senses.example: Microbial growth in the tank was measured every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 罐中的微生物生长每小时测量一次。
senses.why: Growth here is population growth, not the enlargement of one body. The adjective attaches the process to the microbial level, as bacterial growth does for one kind of microbe.
senses.whyCN: 这里的生长是种群增长，而不是单个身体变大；这个形容词把过程固定在微生物层次，正如 bacterial growth 固定于细菌这一类。

senses.title: Microbial Infection
senses.titleCN: 微生物感染的：由微生物侵入引起
senses.definition: caused by microbes entering a host
senses.definitionCN: 由微生物侵入宿主引起的
senses.example: The burns unit screened every patient for microbial infection.
senses.exampleCN: 烧伤病房对每位病人进行微生物感染筛查。
senses.why: In clinical use the adjective can stand in for a cause, like bacterial but broader. The speaker may not yet know which microbe is responsible, so the general term is preferred.
senses.whyCN: 在临床用法中，这个形容词可以像 bacterial 一样表示病因，但范围更宽；说话人可能还不知道是哪种微生物，因此宁用泛称。

senses.title: Microbial Technology
senses.titleCN: 微生物技术的：把微生物当作工具
senses.definition: relating to the use of microbes in technology or industry
senses.definitionCN: 与在技术或工业中利用微生物有关的
senses.example: The microbial fuel cell produced current from waste water.
senses.exampleCN: 微生物燃料电池用废水产生了电流。
senses.why: Here microbes are components of an engineered system. The adjective moves from biology to engineering: the organism is valued for a function it can be made to perform.
senses.whyCN: 这里微生物是工程系统的部件；这个形容词从生物学转向工程学：生物体因其可被安排执行的功能而受重视。

senses.title: Microbial Decomposition
senses.titleCN: 微生物分解的：物质循环中的分解
senses.definition: relating to the breakdown of matter by microbes
senses.definitionCN: 与微生物分解物质有关的
senses.example: Microbial decomposition returned the carbon to the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 微生物分解把碳归还给土壤。
senses.why: Decomposition is a service performed by microbes in every ecosystem. The adjective names the agent of the process, which is why it often appears in ecology and waste treatment.
senses.whyCN: 分解是微生物在每个生态系统中提供的服务；这个形容词命名过程的执行者，因此常出现在生态学与废物处理语境中。

senses.title: Microbial Contamination
senses.titleCN: 微生物污染的：产品或环境被沾染
senses.definition: relating to contamination by microbes
senses.definitionCN: 与微生物造成的污染有关的
senses.example: Microbial contamination closed the bottling line for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 微生物污染使灌装线停工一周。
senses.why: Contamination names the entry of unwanted microbes into a product or a place. The adjective identifies the kind of unwanted life, not the process by which it got in.
senses.whyCN: 污染指不需要的微生物进入产品或场所；这个形容词指明的是不受欢迎的生命种类，而不是它们进入的方式。

intro.en: Microbial is the adjective of microbe, a French coinage of 1878 that was itself built from two Greek elements. Its birth date is known, but its second element was chosen in a way that Greek would not have allowed.
intro.cn: microbial 是 microbe 的形容词，microbe 是 1878 年法语造出的词，本身由两个希腊成分构成。它的生日已知，但第二个成分的选择方式在希腊语里其实并不成立。

items.en: Greek mikros, Attic for smikros, meant 'small'. Its Latinized form micro- became the scientific prefix for the very small. Beekes suggests the Greek word may be Pre-Greek, so its deeper source is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 mikros（阿提卡形式 smikros）意为「小」，其拉丁化形式 micro- 成为表示「极小」的科学前缀。Beekes 认为这个希腊词可能来自前希腊语底层，因此更深来源不确定。

items.en: Greek bios meant 'life, course of life, lifetime', as opposed to zōē, 'animal life'. It supplies the second element of many modern compounds through the combining form bio-.
items.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为「生命、生命历程、寿命」，与表示动物生命的 zōē 相对；它通过组合形式 bio- 为许多现代复合词提供第二成分。

items.en: French microbe was coined in 1878 by the surgeon Charles Sédillot. Etymonline, quoting Weekley, calls it 'badly coined', because in Greek the compound would mean 'short-lived' rather than 'small living thing'. The intended meaning won anyway.
items.cn: 法语 microbe 由外科医生夏尔·塞迪约于 1878 年创制。etymonline 引用 Weekley 的说法称其「造得不好」，因为在希腊语中这个复合词会表示「短命的」，而不是「微小的生物」。但意图中的意义最终胜出。

items.en: Microbial is recorded from 1879, from Modern Latin microbion, the Latinized form of microbe, plus the adjective ending -al. The adjective therefore entered English one year after the noun.
items.cn: microbial 记录于 1879 年，由 microbe 的拉丁化形式现代拉丁 microbion 加形容词词尾 -al 构成；因此形容词比名词晚一年进入英语。

items.en: Microbe was coined as a popular word for disease-causing small life; microorganism, from 1855, is the neutral scientific term. Microbial inherits the popular word's breadth and its medical flavour.
items.cn: microbe 创制时是「致病微小生命」的通俗词，而 1855 年出现的 microorganism 是中性的科学术语。microbial 继承了通俗词的宽泛范围与医学色彩。

items.en: Since the 2000s microbial has appeared in microbial ecology, microbial genetics and microbiome research. In these names it marks a level of biological organisation rather than a single organism.
items.cn: 自本世纪以来，microbial 出现在微生物生态学、微生物遗传学与微生物组研究中；在这些名称里，它标出的是一个生物组织层次，而不是单个生物体。

note.en: The first group holds adjectives and nouns built on the microbe stem. The second group holds overlapping terms whose scope or register differs.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 microbe 词干上的形容词与名词；第二组是范围或语体不同的重叠词。

entries.definition: An older and rarer synonym of microbial, formed with -ic instead of -ial. It appears mainly in nineteenth- and early twentieth-century writing.
entries.definitionCN: microbial 的旧式罕用同义词，用 -ic 而非 -ial 构成；主要见于十九世纪与二十世纪初的文字。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning 'by or with microbes'. It is technical and uncommon outside laboratory writing.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「借微生物作用地」；属于技术用语，实验室文字之外少见。

entries.definition: The study of microbes. The ending -logy marks a field, so it cannot substitute for the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 研究微生物的学科；词尾 -logy 表示领域，不能代替形容词使用。

entries.definition: Of bacteria only. It is the right word when the group is known to be bacterial, and microbial is the right word when fungi or protists may be involved.
entries.definitionCN: 只指细菌的；当已知是细菌时用 bacterial，当可能涉及真菌或原生生物时用 microbial。

entries.definition: Relating to microbiology as a discipline or to its methods, as in microbiological testing. It points to the science, not directly to the organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 与微生物学这一学科或其方法有关的，如微生物学检测；它指向学科，而不是直接指向生物体。

entries.definition: Disease-causing. It says nothing about size or kingdom, and many microbes are not pathogenic.
entries.definitionCN: 指致病的；不涉及大小或生物界，而许多微生物并不致病。

entries.tag: adjective of seeds or early growth
entries.definition: Relating to a germ or seed, or to an early stage of development. It is not a synonym of microbial despite the everyday sense of germ.
entries.definitionCN: 指胚芽、种子或发育早期的；尽管 germ 有「病菌」的日常义，germinal 并不是 microbial 的同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: microbe + -ial: 'having to do with microbes', broader than bacterial.
normal.cn: microbe + -ial：意为「与微生物有关」，范围比 bacterial 更宽。

normal.en: micro- is 'small', bios is 'life'; the compound was meant to say 'small life'.
normal.cn: micro- 是「小」，bios 是「生命」；这个复合词本意是说「微小的生命」。

normal.en: The noun arrived in 1878 and the adjective in 1879, so the pair is almost the same age.
normal.cn: 名词 1878 年出现，形容词 1879 年出现，两者几乎同龄。

normal.en: The family runs microbe, microbes, microbial, microbic, microbially, microbiology and microbiome.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 microbe、microbes、microbial、microbic、microbially、microbiology、microbiome。

normal.en: Use microbial when the kind is unknown or mixed; use bacterial when only bacteria are meant.
normal.cn: 种类未知或混杂时用 microbial；只指细菌时用 bacterial。

abstract.en: Picture a green skin over a wet rock, made of cells too small to name one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象湿岩石上的一层绿皮，由小到无法逐个命名的细胞构成。

abstract.en: Picture a city whose citizens are invisible but whose work keeps the streets clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，市民看不见，而他们的工作让街道保持清洁。

abstract.en: Picture a power station run by creatures you need a lens to meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由必须借助镜片才能见到的生物运转的电站。

examples.en: Microbial activity made the sealed jar swell with gas.
examples.cn: 微生物活动使密封罐因气体而鼓起。

examples.en: The microbial community on the skin protects against some invaders.
examples.cn: 皮肤上的微生物群落能抵御某些入侵者。

examples.en: Microbial contamination was found in three of the sampled bottles.
examples.cn: 抽样检测的瓶子中有三瓶发现了微生物污染。

dict_mnemonic.text: microbe（微生物）+ -ial（与……有关的）→ 与微生物有关的 → microbial 微生物的

root: 希腊 mikros「小」→ 拉丁化 micro- + 希腊 bios「生命」→ 法语 microbe（1878 年塞迪约创制）→ 现代拉丁 microbion → 英语 microbial（microbion + -al，1879）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses attach the adjective to eight objects: the class, life itself, a community, a population, an infection, a technology, a decomposition and a contamination.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个形容词接到八个对象上：类别、生命本身、群落、种群、感染、技术、分解与污染。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slippery green mat over wet rock, made of countless invisible cells.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿岩石上的一层滑绿菌席，由无数看不见的细胞构成。

branches.en: THE CLASS AND LIFE: the broadest relation, then the same adjective applied to life as a form.
branches.cn: 类别与生命：最宽泛的关联，随后同一形容词落在作为一种形态的生命上。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND QUANTITATIVE: a community is organised, while growth is a population count over time.
branches.cn: 集体与数量：群落是有组织的，生长则是种群随时间的计数。

branches.en: HARM: the adjective can name a cause of disease without naming the species.
branches.cn: 危害：这个形容词可以只命名病因，而不指明物种。

branches.en: WORK: microbes are put to work in fuel cells and in the decomposition that recycles matter.
branches.cn: 工作：微生物被用于燃料电池，也用于使物质循环的分解过程。

branches.en: UNWANTED PRESENCE: contamination is the same life arriving where it is not wanted.
branches.cn: 不受欢迎的存在：污染就是同样的生命来到了不该来的地方。

intro.en: Microbial combines a Greek prefix for smallness, a Greek root for life, and a Latin adjective ending, with a Modern Latin noun in between.
intro.cn: microbial 由表示「微小」的希腊前缀、表示「生命」的希腊词根、中间的现代拉丁名词与拉丁形容词词尾组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin microbion Latinized the French microbe before English added -al. There is no classical Latin etymon for microbe; the Latin-looking shape is a modern scientific construction.
latinIntro.cn: 在现代拉丁语中，microbion 把法语 microbe 拉丁化，随后英语加上 -al。microbe 没有古典拉丁语词源；它看似拉丁的外形只是现代科学构造。

items.meaningCN: 微生物的或由微生物引起的
items.exampleCN: 微生物生长充满了培养皿。

items.example: The microbe was cultured from the wound.
items.exampleCN: 从伤口中培养出了这种微生物。

items.example: Microbes colonise the gut at birth.
items.exampleCN: 微生物在出生时定殖于肠道。

items.example: Old texts speak of microbic disease.
items.exampleCN: 旧文献会说到微生物疾病。

items.example: Microbiology examines both harm and use.
items.exampleCN: 微生物学既研究危害也研究用途。

items.meaningCN: 某一地点的微生物群落
items.example: The oral microbiota differs from the gut's.
items.exampleCN: 口腔微生物区系与肠道的不同。

items.meaning: a microbial community and its genes
items.example: The microbiome was sequenced in full.
items.exampleCN: 该微生物组被完整测序。
