definition_zh: 依次、轮流；反过来、进而（表示按顺序相继，或一环引发一环）
definition_en: one after another in order; or as a further consequence, one thing acting back on another
core_image: 一排人依次传递一只水桶，桶从第一双手传到最后一双手
scene: 夜班交接按工位顺序进行，前一岗记录完毕，后一岗才接手清点。 Each shift briefed the next in turn, and the last one reported to the manager.
sceneCN: 这里取「依次、轮流」（第 1 个义项：按顺序相继进行）；句意为各班依次向下一班交接，最后一班向经理汇报。

pos.zh: 副词短语：依次；轮流；反过来

senses.title: One after another
senses.definition: used to say that members of a group do something one after another in a settled order
senses.definitionCN: 表示一群人按既定次序一个接一个地做某事
senses.example: The applications were reviewed in turn by three readers.
senses.exampleCN: 申请材料由三位审阅人依次看过。
senses.why: Turn is a rotation, and a rotation passes each position once before returning.
senses.whyCN: 轮转就是旋转，而旋转让每个位置各经过一次再回到原处。

senses.title: One thing causing the next
senses.definition: used to say that an effect becomes a cause in the next step of a chain
senses.definitionCN: 表示某一后果在链条的下一步又成为原因
senses.example: Higher demand raised prices, which in turn reduced sales.
senses.exampleCN: 需求升高推高了价格，这又反过来压低了销量。
senses.why: In a circle each point hands the motion to the next, which is why turn serves causation as well as order.
senses.whyCN: 在一个圆环上，每一点把运动交给下一点，因此轮转既能表顺序，也能表因果。

senses.title: Not a repayment
senses.definition: it marks succession or consequence, while the look-alike phrase with return marks a response given in exchange
senses.definitionCN: 它标相继或后果，而形近短语标作为交换给出的回应
senses.example: The bank raised rates, and borrowers cut spending in turn.
senses.exampleCN: 银行提高了利率，借款人也随之削减开支。
senses.why: A return travels back to a giver; a turn passes forward along a chain.
senses.whyCN: 回报是回到给予者那里，轮转则沿链条向前传递。

senses.title: Not alternation
senses.definition: it orders a sequence once through, while the phrase with the plural noun describes repeated alternation
senses.definitionCN: 它把序列走一遍，而带复数名词的短语描述反复交替
senses.example: The lights flashed red and green in turn.
senses.exampleCN: 两盏灯依次闪红与绿。
senses.why: A single pass through the positions differs from switching back and forth many times.
senses.whyCN: 把各个位置走一遍，与来回反复切换并不相同。

senses.title: A line of work
senses.definition: in production or administration it describes each station passing work to the next
senses.definitionCN: 在生产或行政中，描述各道工序把工作交给下一道
senses.example: Each station passes the part to the next in turn.
senses.exampleCN: 每道工位依次把零件交给下一道。
senses.why: Assembly is a physical circle of hands, the clearest picture behind the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 装配正是一圈传递的手，这是短语背后最清楚的画面。

senses.title: A chain in an argument
senses.definition: in analysis it links a cause to a further effect, usually inside a relative clause
senses.definitionCN: 在分析中把原因接到更远的后果上，通常出现在定语从句里
senses.example: Funding fell, which in turn slowed the repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 经费削减，这又拖慢了维修。
senses.why: Research prose needs to show chains, and the frame keeps each link visible.
senses.whyCN: 研究文字需要展示链条，这个框架让每一环都看得见。

senses.title: Taking the floor in order
senses.titleCN: 程序义：依次发言或办理
senses.definition: in meetings and formal procedure it means each participant acts in an agreed order
senses.definitionCN: 在会议与正式程序中，指每位参与者按约定次序行事
senses.example: The delegates spoke in turn, each for five minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们依次发言，每人五分钟。
senses.why: Procedure is a rotation of rights, and the phrase keeps the order neutral.
senses.whyCN: 程序是权利的轮转，这个短语让次序保持中性。

senses.title: Not a physical spin
senses.definition: the phrase orders events or effects; it does not describe a wheel or a handle going round
senses.definitionCN: 这个短语排列事件或后果，不描述轮子或把手转动
senses.example: In turn marks order or consequence, never the physical spin of a wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 依次与反过来标记的是顺序或后果，从不指轮子的物理旋转。
senses.why: The noun kept its rotation sense, but the fixed phrase froze only the ordering sense.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了旋转义，但固定短语只冻结了排序义。

intro.en: Turn reached English from Old French torner and Old English turnian, both going back to Latin tornare, to turn on a lathe, from Greek tornos, a lathe. The line is clear; the pre-Greek origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: turn 经古法语 torner 与古英语 turnian 两条线进入英语，两者都可回溯到拉丁语 tornare「在车床上旋削」，再往上为希腊语 tornos「车床」。脉络清楚；这个希腊词更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Tornos named a lathe, the tool that makes a piece turn while a blade cuts it.
items.cn: tornos 指车床，一种让工件旋转、同时用刀切削的工具。

items.en: Where the Greek noun itself came from is disputed, and the source is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个希腊名词本身从何而来尚有争议，来源不确定。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to turn on a lathe and then to turn more generally.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词本指在车床上旋削，后泛指转动。

items.en: A native Old English verb and a French loan merged, giving English one strong turn.
items.cn: 古英语本族动词与法语借词合并，给英语留下一个强势的 turn。

items.en: The ordering and consequence senses are modern developments; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 依次与递进两义属近代发展，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the noun but means response, alternation or strict sequence; the second group are adverbs of succession and linkage.
note.cn: 第一组共用这个名词，却表回报、交替或严格序列；第二组是表相继与连接的副词性说法。

entries.definition: It means as a response or a repayment.
entries.definitionCN: 意为作为回应或回报。

entries.definition: It describes alternating states, often repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 描述交替出现的状态，常反复进行。

entries.definition: It means people replace one another in doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们轮流做某事。

entries.definition: It stresses a fixed order with no idea of effect.
entries.definitionCN: 强调固定顺序，不含相互影响之意。

entries.definition: A single adverb for consecutive items.
entries.definitionCN: 单个副词，表接连发生。

entries.definition: It pairs two lists in the same order.
entries.definitionCN: 把两份列表按同一顺序对应。

entries.definition: It simply moves the narrative to the next step.
entries.definitionCN: 只是把叙述推进到下一步。

entries.definition: It turns the effect into a relative clause.
entries.definitionCN: 把结果写成定语从句。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real lathe root, the real split from return and alternation, and the real chain grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的车床词根、与回报及交替的分工，以及真实的连锁语法。

normal.en: A lathe turns a piece so each side faces the blade once.
normal.cn: 车床让工件转动，使每一面都各对着刀一次。

normal.en: A circle hands motion to the next point, so order becomes cause.
normal.cn: 圆环把运动交给下一点，于是顺序变成因果。

normal.en: Return travels back to a giver; turn travels forward along a chain.
normal.cn: 回报回到给予者，轮转沿链条向前。

normal.en: One pass through the positions is not repeated alternation.
normal.cn: 把位置走一遍，不等于反复交替。

normal.en: The fixed phrase froze the ordering sense and dropped the spin.
normal.cn: 固定短语冻结了排序义，丢掉了旋转义。

abstract.en: Like a bucket passed hand to hand down a line of workers.
abstract.cn: 像水桶在工人队列里一双手一双手地传下去。

abstract.en: Like gears: each wheel moves the next, and the last moves the first.
abstract.cn: 像齿轮：每个轮带动下一个，最后一个又带动第一个。

abstract.en: Like speakers at a long table taking the floor in a fixed order.
abstract.cn: 像长桌旁的人按固定次序依次发言。

examples.en: The three witnesses were questioned in turn.
examples.cn: 三名证人依次受到询问。

examples.en: Cheaper parts cut costs, which in turn raised demand.
examples.cn: 更便宜的零件降低了成本，这又反过来提升了需求。

examples.en: Each member of the panel spoke in turn.
examples.cn: 小组成员依次发言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因 特恩」——水桶一双手一双手往下传：依次、反过来

root: 核心动词意为转动，经古法语 torner 与古英语 turnian 两条线汇合，最终出自拉丁语 tornare「在车床上旋削」，源自希腊语 tornos「车床」；该希腊词更早来源不确定。该短语的依次与递进义为近代发展，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate ordered succession, chained causation, the contrast with return, the contrast with alternation, production lines, argument chains, formal procedure and the exclusion of physical rotation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项区分：有序相继、连锁因果、与回报的对照、与交替的对照、生产线、论证链条、正式程序，以及排除物理旋转。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bucket passed from hand to hand down a line of workers until it reaches the last pair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只水桶在工人队列里一双手传一双手，直到最后一双手。

branches.en: THE SUCCESSION: a line of people or stations takes each position once.
branches.cn: 相继：一列人或工位把每个位置各走一次。

branches.en: THE CHAIN: an effect becomes the cause of the next step, and analysis shows every link.
branches.cn: 连锁：一个后果成为下一步的原因，分析要显示每一环。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: a repayment returns to the giver, not forward along the line.
branches.cn: 对照：回报回到给予者，而非沿队列向前。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: one pass through the positions differs from repeated alternation.
branches.cn: 对照：走一遍位置不同于反复交替。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE AND THE LIMIT: meetings rotate the right to speak, and no wheel is spinning.
branches.cn: 程序与边界：会议轮转发言权，且不指轮子旋转。

intro.en: The phrase is built on a verb that came into English from two directions but from one Latin lathe-word.
intro.cn: 这个短语建在一个动词上，该动词从两个方向进入英语，却同出一个拉丁语车床词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tornare, to turn on a lathe, comes from Greek tornos, a lathe; the Latin verb reached English through French and through native development.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tornare「在车床上旋削」出自希腊语 tornos「车床」；这个拉丁动词经法语与本族发展两条路进入英语。

items.example: The tool that rotates the work while a blade cuts.
items.exampleCN: 一种让工件旋转、同时用刀切削的工具。

items.example: The verb widened from craft to general turning.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词从手艺扩展到一般转动。

items.meaning: to rotate; a rotation; a chance
items.example: English keeps rotation, order and opportunity in one word.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一个词兼指旋转、次序与机会。

items.meaning: a bend; a point of change
items.example: The noun names where a path or an event changes direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指路径或事件转向之处。

items.example: The compound pictures things turning over.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词描绘东西翻过去。

items.example: It names how many come out to an event.
items.exampleCN: 它指有多少人出来参加活动。

items.example: The compound marks a full change of direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词标出方向的整体改变。

items.example: The frame is standard in process description.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架在流程描述中是标准用法。

items.example: The plural form marks repeated switching.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式标出反复切换。

latinEntries.structure: tornare, tornavi, tornatum (verb, first conjugation, from Greek)

definition_zh: n. 徽章；徽记；标记；象征；（界面上的）小角标
definition_en: A small emblem worn to show rank, membership or achievement; a mark taken as a sign of something.
core_image: 别在胸前说明你是谁的那小块金属
scene: 保安别好徽章，站到闸机旁边。 The guard pinned on his badge and stood by the gate.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：badge 指佩戴以表明身份、职级或归属的小徽记。

senses.title: A worn emblem
senses.definition: a small piece of metal, cloth or plastic worn to show rank, job or membership
senses.definitionCN: 佩戴的金属、布或塑料小件，用以表明职级、工作或归属
senses.example: Show your badge at the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 在前台出示你的徽章。
senses.why: Badge began as a heraldic mark identifying a follower of a noble house, so it always answers who you belong to.
senses.whyCN: badge 起初是标识某贵族门下随从的纹章标记，因此它始终回答「你属于谁」。

senses.title: A sign of a quality
senses.definition: a thing taken as evidence of a quality or achievement, whether worn or not
senses.definitionCN: 被视为某种品质或成就之凭证的事物，无论是否佩戴
senses.example: He wore his scars as a badge of courage.
senses.exampleCN: 他把伤疤当作勇气的象征。
senses.why: Because the worn mark proved membership, any proof of a quality could be called a badge.
senses.whyCN: 因为佩戴的标记证明了归属，任何品质的凭证也就都能称为 badge。

senses.title: A small screen marker
senses.definition: in computing, a small number or icon attached to another icon to signal pending items
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机界面中，附于另一图标之上的小数字或小图标，用以提示待处理项
senses.example: A red badge showed nine unread messages.
senses.exampleCN: 一个红色角标显示有九条未读消息。
senses.why: The screen borrowed the worn mark for the same job: a small sign that tells you something waits.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕借用了佩戴标记来做同一件事：一个小提示，告诉你有东西在等着。

intro.en: Badge comes from Middle English bage, a distinguishing mark, whose earlier origin is unknown; it first named the emblem of a noble household.
intro.cn: badge 来自中古英语 bage「识别标记」，更早的来源不明；它最初指贵族门第的徽记。

items.en: Bage is recorded in the fourteenth century for a mark worn by a servant of a lord.
items.cn: bage 于十四世纪有记载，指领主仆从佩戴的标记。

items.en: Such marks identified retainers and were often made of cheap metal in quantity.
items.cn: 这类标记用以识别随从，常以廉价金属大量制作。

items.en: Armies adopted badges of rank and of regiment, fixing the modern shape.
items.cn: 军队采用军衔与团队徽章，确立了现代形态。

items.en: Scouting and schools used badges for skills earned, widening the sense.
items.cn: 童子军与学校用徽章表示已获得的技能，扩展了词义。

items.en: The phrase badge of honour made the word a general sign of a quality.
items.cn: 「荣誉的象征」这一短语使该词成为品质的通用标志。

items.en: Software adopted badge for the small counter attached to an app icon.
items.cn: 软件采用 badge 指附于应用图标上的小计数标记。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words of similar shape; the near-meaning group lists other words for a small identifying sign.
note.cn: 形近组保留形状相近的词；近义组列出表示小型识别标志的其他词。

entries.definition: A burrowing animal, or to pester.
entries.definitionCN: 獾；纠缠不休。

entries.definition: A strip of cloth for a wound.
entries.definitionCN: 包扎伤口的布条。

entries.definition: To move slightly, or to yield.
entries.definitionCN: 略微移动；让步。

entries.definition: To get something by begging.
entries.definitionCN: 靠讨要获得。

entries.definition: A design standing for a group.
entries.definitionCN: 代表某群体的图案。

entries.definition: Marks of rank or office.
entries.definitionCN: 职级或职位的标识。

entries.definition: A thing standing for something else.
entries.definitionCN: 代表他物的东西。

entries.definition: A metal disc given for merit.
entries.definitionCN: 因功绩授予的金属牌。

normalIntro.en: Badge began as the mark of a lord’s follower, so it always says who you belong to or what you have earned.
normalIntro.cn: badge 起初是领主随从的标记，因此它总在说明你属于谁、或你赢得了什么。

normal.en: A badge of honour is the set phrase.
normal.cn: a badge of honour 是固定短语。

normal.en: Name badge and identity badge are workplace terms.
normal.cn: name badge 与 identity badge 是职场用语。

normal.en: Emblem is the design, badge the object.
normal.cn: emblem 指图案，badge 指物件。

normal.en: Insignia is usually plural in use.
normal.cn: insignia 在使用中多为复数。

normal.en: Apps use badge for the little counter.
normal.cn: 应用用 badge 指那个小计数。

abstract.en: Picture a small disc pinned over a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象别在口袋上方的小圆牌。

abstract.en: Imagine a scar read as proof.
abstract.cn: 想象一道被当作凭证的伤疤。

abstract.en: Think of a red dot that will not go away.
abstract.cn: 想象一个怎么也不消失的红点。

examples.en: Her badge gave her access to the lab.
examples.cn: 她的徽章让她能进入实验室。

examples.en: They earned a badge for first aid.
examples.cn: 他们因急救技能获得一枚徽章。

examples.en: The app badge showed three alerts.
examples.cn: 应用角标显示有三条提醒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音记忆：读作「拜纸」——别在胸前那张说明身份的小牌，就是 badge；引申为「象征」，界面小角标也沿用此名。

root: 中古英语 bage「识别标记」来源不明，十四世纪指贵族随从的徽记；后经军队与学校扩展为职级与技能凭证，再引申为品质的象征与界面角标。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are a small sign that speaks for you: worn to show membership, taken as proof of a quality, or attached to an icon.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都是替你说话的小标记：佩戴以表明归属、当作品质的凭证，或附在图标之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small piece of metal on the chest saying who you are
core.cn: 核心意象：别在胸前说明你是谁的那小块金属

branches.en: A guard pinning on his sign.
branches.cn: 别上徽记的保安。

branches.en: A disc granting entry to a lab.
branches.cn: 准予进入实验室的牌子。

branches.en: Scars read as courage.
branches.cn: 被读作勇气的伤疤。

branches.en: A red counter of unread items.
branches.cn: 未读项的红色计数。

branches.en: Both prove something about the wearer.
branches.cn: 两者都证明佩戴者的某种情况。

intro.en: Badge is a single native root; -ing turns it into badging, while Latin signum supplies sign and insignia beside it.
intro.cn: badge 是一个本族词根；-ing 把它变成 badging，而拉丁语 signum 则提供 sign 与 insignia。

latinIntro.en: The word itself is not Latin; Latin signum, mark, gives insignia, and Greek emblema, an inlaid piece, gives emblem.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词本身不属拉丁语；拉丁语 signum「标记」产生 insignia，希腊语 emblema「镶嵌件」产生 emblem。

definition_zh: 水资源保护；节水；通过减少浪费与提高效率来保护水资源的行为与做法
definition_en: the practice and policy of using water carefully so that waste is cut and supplies last for present and future needs
core_image: 一只滴水的水龙头被拧紧，水表上的指针随之慢下来，屋外的水库因此多留下一层水面
scene: 北方城市的社区活动上，志愿者教居民给洗手池换上节水龙头。 Water conservation begins with fixing a single leaking tap.
sceneCN: 这里 water conservation 指「家庭与社区层面减少用水浪费的具体做法」（第 3 个义项：更换器具、修补渗漏等日常节水措施）；句意为节水从修好一个漏水龙头开始。图中可辨识物件：洗手池、节水龙头、扳手、水表。

pos.zh: 水资源保护；节水（不可数名词短语）

senses.title: Careful use so that water is not wasted
senses.definition: the general practice of using water economically so that none is lost unnecessarily
senses.definitionCN: 总体上经济地用水，使水不被无谓流失的做法
senses.example: Water conservation begins with fixing a single leaking tap.
senses.exampleCN: 节水从修好一个漏水龙头开始。
senses.why: Conservation is built on conservare 'to keep safe', so the phrase names keeping a supply safe by not throwing any of it away.
senses.whyCN: conservation 出自 conservare「守住」，因此这个短语指「不把水白白扔掉」来守住储备。

senses.title: Demand management as public policy
senses.titleCN: 作为公共政策的需求管理
senses.definition: the set of rules, prices and programmes by which an authority reduces demand instead of building new supply
senses.definitionCN: 主管机构通过规则、价格与项目压低需求、而非新建供水的一整套办法
senses.example: The city made water conservation the first line of its drought plan.
senses.exampleCN: 该市把节水作为抗旱计划的第一道防线。
senses.why: Once saving a resource becomes a government task, the phrase shifts from household habit to the policy that shapes it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦节约资源成为政府任务，这个短语就从家庭习惯转为塑造习惯的政策。

senses.title: Household and community measures
senses.titleCN: 家庭与社区层面的具体措施
senses.definition: everyday steps such as low-flow fixtures, leak repair, shorter showers and rainwater collection
senses.definitionCN: 低流量器具、修补渗漏、缩短淋浴与收集雨水等日常做法
senses.example: Water conservation in the building cut its bill by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼的节水措施让水费降了三分之一。
senses.why: Policy reaches people as hardware and habit, and this sense names the taps, tanks and timers that carry the idea.
senses.whyCN: 政策以器具和习惯的形式落到人身上，这个义项就指落实这一理念的龙头、水箱与定时器。

senses.title: Irrigation efficiency on farms
senses.titleCN: 农业灌溉中的用水效率
senses.definition: field practices that deliver water to crops with less evaporation, seepage and runoff loss
senses.definitionCN: 减少蒸发、渗漏与径流损失，把水送到作物根部的田间做法
senses.example: Drip lines brought water conservation to the orange groves.
senses.exampleCN: 滴灌带把节水带进了柑橘园。
senses.why: Agriculture takes most of the world's water, so the phrase's largest practical sense is the efficiency of the ditch and the sprinkler.
senses.whyCN: 农业取走世界上大部分水，因此这个短语最大的实用义项就是水渠与喷灌的效率。

senses.title: Industrial reuse and recycling
senses.definition: closed-loop practices in which process water is cleaned and used again rather than discharged
senses.definitionCN: 把工艺用水净化后再次使用、而非直接排放的闭路做法
senses.example: Cooling towers achieved water conservation by cycling the same volume.
senses.exampleCN: 冷却塔靠循环同一批水量实现节水。
senses.why: For a factory the saving is not less use but repeated use, and the phrase covers that loop as well.
senses.whyCN: 对工厂来说，节约不是少用而是反复用，这个短语也涵盖这一循环。

senses.title: Protecting the source and its flows
senses.definition: leaving enough water in rivers, lakes and aquifers to keep ecosystems and downstream users supplied
senses.definitionCN: 在河流、湖泊与含水层中留足水量，以维持生态与下游用水
senses.example: Water conservation also means leaving the river its summer flow.
senses.exampleCN: 节水也意味着给河流留下夏季流量。
senses.why: The oldest sense of conserving is keeping a thing intact; applied to a river, it means not emptying it.
senses.whyCN: conserving 最古老的意义是保持完整；用在河流上，就是不要把它抽空。

senses.title: Storage that keeps water for later
senses.definition: tanks, reservoirs and managed aquifer recharge that hold water through dry periods
senses.definitionCN: 水箱、水库与含水层回补，把水存过干旱期
senses.example: Roof tanks gave the village water conservation through the dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶水箱让村子在旱月里也能存住水。
senses.why: Keeping water safe includes keeping it somewhere, so storage belongs to the same family of meanings as not wasting it.
senses.whyCN: 把水守住也包括把水存放在某处，因此蓄水与「不浪费」属于同一族含义。

senses.title: Abstract: prudent use of any shared resource
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：像省水一样节制使用共有资源
senses.definition: a transferred use for careful, sparing management of any limited shared resource
senses.definitionCN: 转指对任何有限共有资源进行细心、节制管理
senses.example: The team applied water conservation habits to its own meeting time.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队把节水的习惯用到自己的会议时间上。
senses.why: The metaphor survives because the shape is general: a finite pool, many users, and a rule against waste.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻能成立，是因为形态是通用的：有限的池子、许多使用者，以及一条不许浪费的规矩。

intro.en: Water conservation joins the native English word water to a Latin-derived noun of keeping safe. The phrase itself is a modern English construction, transparent in meaning. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: water conservation 把英语本族词 water 与拉丁来源的「守住」名词连在一起。这个短语本身是近代英语构造，含义透明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wæter is the native word for water, recorded from the earliest English. Its deeper origin is not established; the common Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: wæter 是英语最早期就有记录的本族「水」词。其更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的印欧形式是重构，而非有书证的词。

items.en: Servare meant 'to keep, watch over, guard'. Its own deeper origin is unsettled; the link sometimes drawn to servire 'to serve' is a hypothesis rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: servare 意为「看守、保存、守护」。其更深来源无定论；有人把它与 servire「服侍」联系起来，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Com- 'thoroughly, together' plus servare produced conservare 'to keep safe, maintain'; the noun conservatio named the act.
items.cn: com-「彻底、共同」加 servare 构成 conservare「保住、维持」；名词 conservatio 指这一动作。

items.en: Old French conserver brought the verb into English in the fourteenth century, and conservation first named the preserving of health, goods or rights.
items.cn: 古法语 conserver 在十四世纪把动词带入英语，conservation 最初指对健康、财物或权利的保全。

items.en: Water and conservation were joined in English writing on resource management, first for forests and soils and then for rivers and city supply.
items.cn: water 与 conservation 在英语资源管理写作中连用，先用于森林与土壤，后用于河流与城市供水。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the compound, deeper origin of wæter and servare): no single earliest citation is fixed for the phrase, so its first date is approximate; the pre-English origin of wæter and the pre-Latin origin of servare are unsettled, and any forms offered for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该短语的首见年代，以及 wæter 与 servare 的更深词源）：这个短语没有公认的最早书证，首见年代只能约计；wæter 在英语之前的来源与 servare 在拉丁语之前的来源均无定论，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built on conserve or on the word water that name neighbouring but distinct ideas; group two holds terms from water management that are regularly substituted for this one.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 conserve 或同含 water、但所指相邻而不同的短语；第二组是水管理领域中常被拿来替换本短语的术语。

entries.definition: The ratio of useful water delivered to water taken; it is a performance figure, while conservation is the wider practice that aims at it.
entries.definitionCN: 有效供水与取水之比；它是一个绩效数字，而 conservation 是追求这一数字的更宽泛做法。

entries.definition: The plain everyday phrase for using less water, usually of devices and habits rather than of policy.
entries.definitionCN: 指少用水的日常说法，通常用于器具与习惯，而不用于政策。

entries.definition: Keeping water fit to use, as in stored samples; preservation guards quality, while conservation guards quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 保持水可使用，如保存水样；preservation 护的是质量，conservation 护的是数量。

entries.definition: Protection of soil from erosion and loss; the construction is identical but the resource is different.
entries.definitionCN: 保护土壤不受侵蚀与流失；构造完全相同，但所护资源不同。

entries.definition: The utility's term for reducing consumption by pricing, rules and retrofits; water conservation is the public-facing name for the same effort.
entries.definitionCN: 供水机构对通过价格、规则与改造压低用水的称呼；water conservation 是同一努力面向公众的名字。

entries.definition: Sending treated water back into a second use; it is one method within conservation rather than the whole policy.
entries.definitionCN: 把处理过的水送入第二次用途；它是节水中的一种方法，而非整套政策。

entries.definition: Repeated use of the same water in a process; it overlaps with conservation but stresses the loop rather than the saving.
entries.definitionCN: 同一批水在工艺中反复使用；它与节水重叠，但强调循环而非节约。

entries.definition: The general protection of any resource; the phrase simply fixes that noun to water.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指对任何资源的保护；本短语只是把这个名词限定到水。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Conservation is com- 'thoroughly' plus servare 'keep safe': keeping a supply safe all round.
normal.cn: conservation 是 com-「彻底」加 servare「守住」：把储备整个护住。

normal.en: The phrase is simply conservation applied to water, as soil conservation applies it to soil.
normal.cn: 这个短语就是把 conservation 用在水上，正如 soil conservation 用在土上。

normal.en: The family runs conserve, conservation, conservationist, conservative and conservancy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 conserve、conservation、conservationist、conservative 与 conservancy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the practice: water conservation measures, water conservation program, household water conservation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出做法：节水措施、节水计划、家庭节水。

normal.en: The everyday counterpart is written as a compound adjective: water-saving taps, water-conservation technology.
normal.cn: 日常对应说法写作复合形容词：节水龙头、节水技术。

abstract.en: Picture a tap turned just past the drip, and a reservoir that keeps one extra layer of water.
abstract.cn: 想象水龙头被拧过滴水的位置，水库因此多留了一层水面。

abstract.en: Picture a shared jug at a table where everyone pours a little less.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上共用的水壶，每个人都少倒一点。

abstract.en: Picture a budget in which saving is not a loss but a reserve kept for a dry day.
abstract.cn: 想象一本预算，省下的不是损失，而是留给旱日的储备。

examples.en: Water conservation measures cut the city's demand by nearly a fifth.
examples.cn: 节水措施把全市用水需求削减了近五分之一。

examples.en: Farmers turned to water conservation when the wells began to fail.
examples.cn: 水井开始枯竭时，农民转向节水。

examples.en: The school runs a water conservation campaign every spring.
examples.cn: 这所学校每年春天开展节水宣传。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「water（水）+ conservation（保护）」——把水守住，别让它白白流走 → 节水、水资源保护

root: 英语复合短语：water 来自古英语 wæter「水」，更深来源不确定；conservation 来自拉丁 conservare「保住、维持」= com-（彻底）+ servare「守住」，servare 更深来源亦无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rule: take less, lose less, use it again, keep the source full and store what is spared. The last sense applies that rule to any shared pool.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条规则展开：少取、少漏、再用、让水源保持充盈、把省下的存起来。最后一个义项把这条规则用到任何共用的池子上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dripping tap is closed and the level in the reservoir stops falling.
core.cn: 核心意象：滴水龙头被拧紧，水库的水位不再下降。

branches.en: SAVING: personal habit and public policy are the same rule at two scales.
branches.cn: 节约：个人习惯与公共政策是同一条规则在两个尺度上。

branches.en: DEVICES AND FIELDS: taps, showers, drip lines and schedules all deliver the saving.
branches.cn: 器具与田间：龙头、淋浴、滴灌带与灌溉安排都在落实节约。

branches.en: LOOP: industry saves by using the same water twice rather than by using less.
branches.cn: 循环：工业靠同一批水用两次来节约，而不是靠少用。

branches.en: KEEPING INTACT: a river left with its flow and a tank kept full are both stores held safe.
branches.cn: 保持完整：给河流留流量、把水箱存满，都是把储备守住。

branches.en: TRANSFER: any finite shared pool can be managed by the same rule.
branches.cn: 转移：任何有限的共有池子都能用同一条规则管理。

intro.en: The phrase combines a native English noun with a Latin-derived noun of two morphemes, so it can be read as an English compound and as a Latin family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由英语本族名词与一个含两个语素的拉丁来源名词构成，因此既可当作英语复合词读，也可当作一个拉丁词族读。

latinIntro.en: Latin servare gives conserve, conservation, conservator, preserve, reserve and observe; com- adds 'thoroughly, together'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 servare 衍生 conserve、conservation、conservator、preserve、reserve 与 observe；com- 增添「彻底、共同」。

items.example: The water in the tank lasted all summer.
items.exampleCN: 水箱里的水撑过了整个夏天。

items.example: The prefix binds the keeping into one whole act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「守住」收束为一个整体动作。

items.structure: servare, servavi, servatum (Latin verb, 'to keep, guard')
items.example: The root carries the idea of keeping watch.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「看守」的意思。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: The conservation of the old mill took years.
items.exampleCN: 这座老磨坊的保护工作花了多年。

items.meaning: to keep safe; to use sparingly
items.example: They conserve water in the dry season.

items.meaning: tending to keep things as they are
items.meaningCN: 倾向维持原状的；保守的

items.meaning: a person who works to protect nature
items.exampleCN: 这位保护者标出了泉眼位置。

definition_zh: adj. 明确无疑的，绝对的；范畴的，分类的
definition_en: stated in a direct and certain way, with no doubt allowed; relating to categories
core_image: 一句话斩钉截铁，不留余地
scene: 发言人明确表示，这类请求一律拒绝。 The spokesman gave a categorical refusal of every such request.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：categorical 指明确无疑的；句意是发言人一口拒绝所有这类请求。

senses.title: Said without doubt
senses.definition: expressed clearly and with no possibility of exception
senses.definitionCN: 表达清楚，不允许任何例外
senses.example: The minister issued a categorical denial.
senses.exampleCN: 部长断然否认。
senses.why: The word came from Greek kategorikos, said of a statement, from kategorein, to assert.
senses.whyCN: 该词源自希腊语 kategorikos（关于陈述的），来自 kategorein（断言）。

senses.title: Of categories
senses.definition: relating to a class or to logical categories
senses.definitionCN: 与类别或逻辑范畴有关的
senses.example: The two claims are categorical rather than historical.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个主张属于范畴层面而非历史层面。
senses.why: Philosophy kept the older sense of naming and classifying.
senses.whyCN: 哲学保留了命名与分类的旧义。

intro.en: Categorical comes from Greek kategorikos, from kategorein, to assert or accuse in public.
intro.cn: categorical 源自希腊语 kategorikos，来自 kategorein（公开断言或指控）。

items.en: Kategorein means to assert in public.
items.cn: kategorein 意为公开断言。

items.en: Kategoria names a class or a statement.
items.cn: kategoria 指类别或陈述。

items.en: Logic borrows categorical for direct statements.
items.cn: 十五世纪逻辑学用 categorical 指直接陈述。

items.en: Kant names the categorical imperative.
items.cn: 十八世纪康德提出绝对命令。

items.en: Everyday speech keeps the sense of no doubt.
items.cn: 现代日常用法保留毫无疑问义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the categor- stem; the near-meaning group separates firm statements from cautious ones.
note.cn: 形近组共享 categor- 词干；近义组区分坚定陈述与谨慎表述。

entries.definition: A class of things.
entries.definitionCN: 类别。

entries.definition: To place things in classes.
entries.definitionCN: 分类。

entries.definition: A shorter adjective form.
entries.definitionCN: 明确的（简式）。

entries.definition: Complete and without limit.
entries.definitionCN: 绝对的。

entries.definition: Not limited by conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 无条件的。

entries.definition: Said with force.
entries.definitionCN: 强调的。

normalIntro.en: A categorical answer is one filed under no exceptions.
normalIntro.cn: categorical 的回答会被归入没有例外这一类别。

normal.en: Kategoria meant a class.
normal.cn: kategoria 指类别。

normal.en: Logic used it for direct statements.
normal.cn: 逻辑学用它指直接陈述。

normal.en: A categorical denial leaves no room.
normal.cn: 断然否认不留余地。

normal.en: Kant made the imperative famous.
normal.cn: 康德让绝对命令广为人知。

normal.en: The adjective keeps both senses.
normal.cn: 这个形容词兼有两种含义。

abstract.en: A door closed with one clean click.
abstract.cn: 一声干脆落锁的门。

abstract.en: A sentence with no back door.
abstract.cn: 一句没有后门的话。

abstract.en: A label that forbids relabelling.
abstract.cn: 禁止再贴标签的标签。

examples.en: The minister issued a categorical denial.
examples.cn: 部长发表了断然否认。

examples.en: He was categorical about the deadline.
examples.cn: 他对截止期限说得斩钉截铁。

examples.en: She categorically denied the charge.
examples.cn: 她断然否认了这项指控。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡台哥瑞扣」——把话卡在台面上，一锤定音，绝不改口。

root: 希腊语 kategorein（公开断言）→ kategorikos → 英语 categorical

sensesIntro.en: Asserting and classifying are the same old word seen from two angles.
sensesIntro.cn: 断言与分类，是同一个古老词语的两个侧面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence nailed flat to the table
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话被钉平在桌面上

branches.en: A refusal that ends the discussion.
branches.cn: 一句结束讨论的拒绝。

branches.en: A promise with no conditions.
branches.cn: 一个没有条件的承诺。

branches.en: A claim about kinds, not cases.
branches.cn: 关于类别而非个案的论断。

branches.en: A philosopher sorting predicates.
branches.cn: 哲学家整理谓词。

branches.en: Certainty organised into classes.
branches.cn: 被整理进类别的确定性。

intro.en: Categorical carries a Greek root; the list below adds words for speech, logic and classes.
intro.cn: categorical 带有希腊词根；下面列出言语、逻辑、类别词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek kategorein is to assert, and Latin dicere is to say.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kategorein 意为断言，拉丁语 dicere 意为说。

latinEntries.exampleCN: kategoria 产生 category 与 categorical。
dicere 产生 dictate 与 verdict。
classis 产生 class 与 classify。

definition_zh: 吸收；吸附；（营养的）摄取；专注；并入；吸收（光、热、声）；吸附作用
definition_en: the taking in of a liquid, gas, nutrient, energy, or knowledge, and the state of being completely engaged or merged into something larger
core_image: 一块干海绵贴到水面上，水沿着孔隙往上走，表面很快变暗变重。
scene: 雨刚停，田里那块黏土地还按着水不放，农机一开进去就打了滑。 The absorption of water by the clay soil delayed the planting.
sceneCN: 这里 absorption 是「材料对水的吸收」（第 1 个义项）；句意：黏土对水的吸收延误了播种。场景：雨后的田、脚陷进去的泥、拖拉机留下的深辙。

senses.title: The uptake of liquid by a material
senses.definition: the process by which a solid takes a liquid into itself, filling its pores or spaces
senses.definitionCN: 固体把液体纳入自身、填满孔隙或空隙的过程
senses.example: The absorption of water by the clay soil delayed the planting.
senses.exampleCN: 黏土对水的吸收延误了播种。
senses.why: Latin absorbere is to suck in. The image is not a surface coating but a material pulling something inside itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absorbere 是“吸进去”。画面不是表面涂层，而是材料把某物拉进自身内部。

senses.title: The body's uptake of nutrients
senses.titleCN: 吸收营养：穿过肠壁进了身体
senses.definition: the passage of digested nutrients into the blood or body tissues
senses.definitionCN: 消化后的营养进入血液或身体组织的过程
senses.example: Poor absorption of iron can cause fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 铁吸收不良会导致疲劳。
senses.why: The body is the container here. Nutrients are not merely eaten but taken through a wall into the interior.
senses.whyCN: 这里的容器是身体。营养不只是被吃下，而是穿过一道壁进入内部。

senses.title: The taking in of knowledge
senses.titleCN: 知识的吸收：读进去、化成自己的
senses.definition: the process of understanding and remembering information so that it becomes part of one's knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 理解并记住信息，使其成为自身知识一部分的过程
senses.example: The course depends on steady absorption of new vocabulary.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课依赖对新词汇的稳定吸收。
senses.why: Learning is treated as a material process: what is read is absorbed into the mind as water is absorbed into a cloth.
senses.whyCN: 学习被当作材料过程：读到的东西被吸进心里，就像水被吸进布中。

senses.title: Complete engrossment in an activity
senses.titleCN: 专注：整个人被吸进一件事
senses.definition: the state of having all one's attention taken by something, so that time and surroundings drop away
senses.definitionCN: 全部注意力被某事物占据，时间与周围环境都退去的状态
senses.example: His absorption in the problem made him miss the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那个问题的专注让他错过了末班车。
senses.why: The same verb that takes liquid into a sponge takes a person into a task. The mind has no attention left on the surface.
senses.whyCN: 把水吸进海绵的那个动词，也把人吸进一项任务。心智在表面上再没留下注意力。

senses.title: The merging of an organisation
senses.titleCN: 并入：小公司被大公司吞进去
senses.definition: the incorporation of one company, group, or territory into a larger one, losing separate identity
senses.definitionCN: 一个公司、团体或地区被并入更大者，失去独立身份
senses.example: The absorption of the smaller firm took two years to complete.
senses.exampleCN: 对那家较小公司的并入花了两年才完成。
senses.why: Corporate absorption keeps the physical picture: the smaller body is taken inside the larger and no longer has an outer surface of its own.
senses.whyCN: 公司“并入”保留了物理画面：较小的实体被纳入更大者内部，不再有自己的外表面。

senses.title: The uptake of light or energy
senses.definition: the process in which matter takes up electromagnetic radiation or energy, often converting it into heat
senses.definitionCN: 物质摄取电磁辐射或能量、常将其转为热的过程
senses.example: The dark surface showed strong absorption across the visible spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 深色表面在整个可见光谱上表现出强吸收。
senses.why: Physics names with the old verb: a photon is not reflected or transmitted but swallowed by the material.
senses.whyCN: 物理学沿用这个古老动词：光子不被反射或透射，而是被材料吞掉。

senses.title: The dissolving of a gas in a liquid
senses.titleCN: 溶解吸收：气体进了液体里面
senses.definition: the process by which gas molecules enter the bulk of a liquid rather than staying on its surface
senses.definitionCN: 气体分子进入液体内部、而非停留在表面的过程
senses.example: The absorption of carbon dioxide by seawater lowers the ocean's pH.
senses.exampleCN: 海水对二氧化碳的吸收降低了海洋的 pH。
senses.why: Chemistry distinguishes absorption from adsorption: here the gas goes inside the liquid, not onto a surface.
senses.whyCN: 化学区分 absorption 与 adsorption：这里气体进入液体内部，而不是附着在表面。

senses.title: The damping of sound
senses.definition: the reduction of sound energy as it passes into a material, so that less is reflected back
senses.definitionCN: 声音进入材料时能量被削减、反射回来的部分减少
senses.example: The studio's walls were chosen for their low-frequency absorption.
senses.exampleCN: 录音室的墙是按低频吸声性能挑选的。
senses.why: Sound is a wave, and a porous wall takes part of it in. The energy does not vanish; it becomes a little heat inside the material.
senses.whyCN: 声音是波，多孔的墙把其中一部分收进去。能量并未消失，而是在材料内部变成一点热。

intro.en: Absorption is Latin absorptio, from absorbere 'to suck in': ab- 'away' plus sorbere 'to suck'. English borrowed the noun in the 16c and later gave it technical work in physics and chemistry.
intro.cn: absorption 是拉丁语 absorptio，来自 absorbere“吸进去”：ab-“离开”加 sorbere“吸”。英语 16 世纪借入这个名词，后来才在物理与化学中给它技术任务。

items.en: To suck in, swallow, or drink up. It describes a mouth or a porous body drawing something inward.
items.cn: 吸入、吞下、喝干。它描述嘴或多孔的身体把某物向内拉。

items.en: Away from, off. With sorbere it marks the movement of something out of its surroundings and into the absorbing body.
items.cn: 离开、脱离。与 sorbere 结合，标记某物从周围环境进入吸收者内部。

items.en: To swallow up, to take in completely. It is used of the sea swallowing a ship as well as of a sponge taking water.
items.cn: 吞没、完全纳入。它既用于大海吞没船只，也用于海绵吸水。

items.en: A swallowing up. The noun is rare in classical Latin but exactly matches the English technical need.
items.cn: 吞没、吸尽。这个名词在古典拉丁语中不常见，却正好对应英语的技术需要。

items.en: The noun enters English through learned writing. Early uses are medical and alchemical before they become physical.
items.cn: 这个名词经学术写作进入英语。早期用法属医学与炼金术，之后才转为物理学用法。

items.en: Physics, chemistry, acoustics, and business each take a share: light, gas, sound, nutrients, and companies are all absorbed. The mental sense, absorbed in a book, keeps the oldest metaphor alive.
items.cn: 物理学、化学、声学与商业各取一份：光、气体、声音、营养、公司都能被“吸收”。心智义“沉浸在一本书里”让最古老的比喻继续活着。

note.en: The first group is the absorb family plus adsorption, a look-alike with a different prefix and a genuinely different process; the second compares other kinds of taking in.
note.cn: 第一组是 absorb 词族，外加 adsorption——一个前缀不同、过程也确实不同的形近词；第二组比较其他“纳入”方式。

entries.definition: to take in liquid, energy, or information. The verb is the act; absorption is the process or state.
entries.definitionCN: 吸收液体、能量或信息；动词指动作，absorption 指过程或状态。

entries.definition: able to absorb, or a material that does so. It describes capacity, not an event.
entries.definitionCN: 能吸收的，或指吸收材料；描述能力，而非事件。

entries.definition: relating to absorption. It often appears in technical phrases such as absorptive capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 与吸收有关的，常见于 absorptive capacity 等技术短语。

entries.definition: the sticking of molecules onto a surface. It uses ad- 'to' rather than ab- 'away', and is a surface process, not an uptake into the bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 分子附着在表面。它用 ad-“向”而非 ab-“离开”，是表面过程，不是吸入内部。

entries.definition: the taking in of a substance by a cell, tissue, or system. It is the neutral scientific partner.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞、组织或系统对物质的摄取；是中性的科学伙伴。

entries.definition: the process of absorbing information or a group so that it becomes part of the whole. It stresses integration after uptake.
entries.definitionCN: 把信息或群体吸收进来、使之成为整体一部分；强调摄入之后的整合。

entries.definition: the formal merging of one body into another. It is the legal form of the corporate sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一个实体正式并入另一个；是公司义的法律形式。

entries.definition: the state of having one's attention completely occupied. It is the mental sense without the physical image.
entries.definitionCN: 注意力被完全占据的状态；是去掉物理意象的心智义。

entries.definition: the reduction in strength of a signal or wave. It names the result of acoustic absorption, not the taking in.
entries.definitionCN: 信号或波强度的减弱；命名吸声的结果，而非“吸进去”的动作。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ab- 'away' plus sorbere 'to suck'. The same root gives absorb, absorbent, and absorptive; adsorption is a different prefix and a different process.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ab-“离开”加 sorbere“吸”。同一词根给出 absorb、absorbent、absorptive；adsorption 前缀不同，过程也不同。

normal.en: Ab- away, sorb suck: absorption is something sucked away into another body.
normal.cn: ab- 离开，sorb 吸：absorption 就是某物被吸走、进入另一个物体。

normal.en: A sponge does not coat itself with water; it pulls the water inside.
normal.cn: 海绵不是给自己涂上一层水，而是把水拉进内部。

normal.en: Adsorption sticks to the surface; absorption goes into the bulk. One letter, two processes.
normal.cn: adsorption 贴在表面，absorption 进入内部。差一个字母，是两种过程。

normal.en: Absorbed in a book: the reader has been taken inside the text.
normal.cn: absorbed in a book：读者被吸进文本里面。

normal.en: A dark wall absorbs light and turns it into a little heat.
normal.cn: 深色的墙吸收光，并把它变成一点热。

abstract.en: Absorption is what happens when a boundary lets something through instead of bouncing it back.
abstract.cn: 吸收，就是边界让某物通过、而不是把它弹回去。

abstract.en: To be absorbed is to have no surface left for the world.
abstract.cn: 被吸进去，就是再没有留给世界的表面。

abstract.en: Matter, mind, and companies all have pores.
abstract.cn: 物质、心智与公司，都有孔隙。

examples.en: The root hairs increase the absorption of water from the soil.
examples.cn: 根毛增加了对土壤中水的吸收。

examples.en: His absorption in the chess game made the room seem to disappear.
examples.cn: 他对棋局的专注让整个房间仿佛消失了。

examples.en: The fabric's sound absorption was measured in a test chamber.
examples.cn: 这种织物的吸声性能在测试舱中被测量。

dict_mnemonic.text: “额不吸哦普申”——海绵“额”一下把水吸进去 → absorption 吸收

root: 源自拉丁语 absorptio，来自 absorbere（ab-“离开”+ sorbere“吸、吞”），本义“吸进去、吞没”；核心是“把外部之物纳入内部”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of absorption, one movement: something outside passes a boundary and becomes part of what is inside. The boundary can be a pore, a gut wall, a mind, a company, or a surface.
sensesIntro.cn: absorption 的八个义项只有一个动作：外部之物越过一道边界，成为内部的一部分。边界可以是孔隙、肠壁、心智、公司，或一个表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry sponge touching water and pulling it up into its pores.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块干海绵触到水面，把水往上拉进孔里。

branches.en: MATERIAL UPTAKE: a sponge and a seawater sample both pull a substance inside, one through pores and one through a liquid surface.
branches.cn: 材料摄入：海绵与海水样本都把物质拉进内部，一个经孔隙，一个经液面。

branches.en: THE BODY: nutrients cross a wall and become part of the organism.
branches.cn: 身体：营养穿过一道壁，成为生物体的一部分。

branches.en: THE MIND: knowledge is taken in, and a task can take the whole person in.
branches.cn: 心智：知识被吸进去，一项任务也能把整个人吸进去。

branches.en: THE ORGANISATION: a smaller firm loses its outer surface inside a larger one.
branches.cn: 组织：较小的公司在更大者内部失去自己的外表面。

branches.en: ENERGY AND SOUND: light and sound are swallowed and turned into heat rather than sent back.
branches.cn: 能量与声音：光与声被吞下、转为热，而不是被送回。

intro.en: Absorption carries Latin ab- and -tion. English builds the verb absorb, the capacity adjective absorbent, and the relational adjective absorptive.
intro.cn: absorption 带着拉丁前缀 ab- 与后缀 -tion。英语造出动词 absorb、能力形容词 absorbent，以及关系形容词 absorptive。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is sorbere 'to suck', absorbere 'to suck in', and absorptio 'a swallowing up'. Adsorption is not in this chain: it uses ad- and means surface attachment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 sorbere“吸”、absorbere“吸进去”、absorptio“吞没”。adsorption 不在这个链条里：它用 ad-，意为表面附着。

items.meaning: to take in liquid, energy, or information
items.meaningCN: 吸收液体、能量或信息（拉丁动词英语化）
items.example: The paper towel absorbed the spill.
items.exampleCN: 纸巾吸干了洒出来的液体。

items.meaning: able to absorb; a material that absorbs
items.meaningCN: 能吸收的；吸收材料（-ent 构成形容词或名词）
与吸收有关的（-ive 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The absorptive capacity of the soil is low.
items.exampleCN: 这种土壤的吸收能力很低。

items.meaning: the process or state of being absorbed
items.meaningCN: 吸收的过程或被吸收的状态（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Absorption of the drug is fastest on an empty stomach.

items.meaningCN: 自我专注；只顾自己（复合名词）
items.exampleCN: 他的自我专注让团队合作变得困难。

items.meaning: the pattern of wavelengths a substance takes in
items.meaningCN: 物质所吸收波长的图谱（技术复合词）
items.example: The absorption spectrum identified the gas.
items.exampleCN: 吸收光谱确定了这种气体。

items.meaning: the speed at which a substance is taken in
items.meaningCN: 物质被吸收的速度（技术复合词）
items.example: The absorption rate depends on temperature.

items.meaning: the uptake of water by a material or body
items.meaningCN: 材料或身体对水的吸收（固定短语）
items.example: The absorption of water by the seeds begins within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 种子对水的吸收在几分钟内就开始。

items.meaning: the damping of sound energy by a material
items.meaningCN: 材料对声能的削减（复合词）
items.example: The ceiling panels improve sound absorption.
items.exampleCN: 天花板板材改善了吸声效果。

items.meaning: the merging of a firm into another
items.meaningCN: 一家公司被并入另一家（商业短语）
items.example: The absorption of the company removed its brand from the market.
items.exampleCN: 该公司的并入使其品牌从市场上消失。

definition_zh: 拥护者；信徒；黏附的；附着物
definition_en: a supporter of a cause, person or belief, or something that sticks firmly to a surface
core_image: 标签紧紧贴在玻璃上，怎么撕都撕不下来
scene: 新贴的标签粘在瓶身上，冲洗几次也没有脱落。 The adherent refused to abandon the movement.
sceneCN: 这里 adherent 是「拥护者」（第 1 个义项：坚定支持某项事业的人）；句意为这名拥护者拒绝放弃这项运动。

pos.zh: 名词：拥护者；信徒；附着物

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「黏附；坚持」
由动词加 -ence 构成，义为「黏附；坚持；遵奉」
由拉丁分词加 -ion 构成，义为「黏附；附着力」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「黏合剂；胶带」

senses.title: A supporter of a cause
senses.definition: a person who supports a movement, leader or idea and remains loyal to it
senses.definitionCN: 支持某项运动、某位领袖或某种理念并保持忠诚的人
senses.example: The movement gained adherents in every large city.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动在每座大城市都赢得了拥护者。
senses.why: Adhere means to stick to, and a supporter sticks to a cause, so the physical image becomes a political one.
senses.whyCN: adhere 意为「黏住」，支持者会「黏」在一项事业上，于是物理画面变成了政治画面。

senses.title: A follower of a religion
senses.definition: a person who follows a particular faith, teacher or religious tradition
senses.definitionCN: 追随某一信仰、导师或宗教传统的人
senses.example: Adherents of the tradition gather there each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这一传统的信徒每年春天在那里聚会。
senses.why: Faith is something a person holds fast to, so the word for sticking becomes the word for religious belonging.
senses.whyCN: 信仰是人紧紧抓住的东西，所以表示「黏附」的词变成了表示宗教归属的词。

senses.title: Sticking firmly to a surface
senses.definition: describing a layer or substance that remains firmly attached to a surface
senses.definitionCN: 形容某层物质牢固附着在表面上
senses.example: The adherent film survived repeated washing.
senses.exampleCN: 这层附着膜经受了反复冲洗。
senses.why: The literal physical sense is the root image: two surfaces held together by contact.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的物理义是根本画面：两个表面靠接触被粘在一起。

senses.title: Adherent cells in biology
senses.definition: cells that attach to the surface of a culture vessel in order to grow
senses.definitionCN: 为生长而附着在培养容器表面的细胞
senses.example: The lab studies adherent cells that need a surface to spread.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室研究需要表面才能铺展的贴壁细胞。
senses.why: Cells that must stick to a dish are literally adherent, so biology borrows the everyday adjective.
senses.whyCN: 必须粘在培养皿上的细胞字面上就是「附着的」，所以生物学借用了这个日常形容词。

senses.title: A strict follower of rules
senses.definition: a person who keeps closely to a rule, principle or doctrine
senses.definitionCN: 紧密遵循某项规则、原则或教义的人
senses.example: He is an adherent of the old method and will not change.
senses.exampleCN: 他是旧方法的坚定遵循者，不愿改变。
senses.why: To adhere to a rule is to stay attached to it, which produces the sense of strict loyalty.
senses.whyCN: adhere to a rule 就是「黏在规则上」，于是产生了严格忠诚的含义。

senses.title: A political loyalist
senses.definition: a person who remains loyal to a party or political leader through difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 在困难时期仍忠于某政党或政治领袖的人
senses.example: The senator's adherents defended him after the scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻之后，这位参议员的追随者仍为他辩护。
senses.why: Politics tests loyalty, so the sticking image is used for those who do not peel away.
senses.whyCN: 政治考验忠诚，所以「黏住」的画面被用来指那些没有脱落的人。

senses.title: Attached by adhesion
senses.definition: in engineering, describing parts joined by molecular attraction rather than by bolts
senses.definitionCN: 工程中指靠分子吸引力而非螺栓连接的部件
senses.example: The adherent joint failed when the surface was wet.
senses.exampleCN: 表面潮湿时，这个黏附连接失效了。
senses.why: Engineering needs a word for contact-based joining, and adherent supplies it directly.
senses.whyCN: 工程需要为「靠接触连接」命名，adherent 正好直接提供这个词。

senses.title: An attached layer in materials
senses.definition: a thin layer that stays bonded to a substrate, as in coatings or films
senses.definitionCN: 保持在基底上的薄层，如涂层或薄膜
senses.example: The adherent layer protects the metal beneath.
senses.exampleCN: 这层附着层保护下面的金属。
senses.why: Coating work speaks of layers that must not peel, which extends the physical sense to materials science.
senses.whyCN: 涂装工艺讲的是不能剥落的层，这把物理义延伸到材料科学。

intro.en: Adherent comes from the Latin verb for sticking to something, and its two senses grew from one physical image.
intro.cn: adherent 来自拉丁语表示「黏在……上」的动词，它的两个义项都从同一个物理画面长出。

items.en: Haerere meant to stick, cling or remain fixed; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: haerere 意为「黏住、附着、固定不动」，其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Ad plus haerere formed adhaerere, to stick to or cleave to something.
items.cn: ad 与 haerere 构成 adhaerere，意为「黏到、附着于某物」。

items.en: The present participle adhaerens meant sticking to, and it is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 现在分词 adhaerens 意为「黏着的」，是英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French adherent carried the word into English with both the physical and the loyal senses.
items.cn: 古法语 adherent 把这个词带入英语，物理义与忠诚义同时进入。

items.en: The word is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Science added the technical senses for cells, joints and coatings, all keeping the idea of staying attached.
items.cn: 科学增加了细胞、接头与涂层等技术义项，但都保留「保持附着」的理念。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adhere family; the near-meaning group gathers supporters and sticky terms with different focus.
note.cn: 形近组收 adhere 词族；近义组收支持者与黏性词，侧重点不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to stick to a surface or to follow a rule closely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「黏附」或「坚持遵循」。

entries.definition: The noun for sticking to something or following a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黏附」或「遵循」。

entries.definition: The physical force by which surfaces stay attached.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黏附、附着力」，指表面保持贴合的力量。

entries.definition: A substance that sticks things together, such as glue or tape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「黏合剂、胶带」或「黏性的」。

entries.definition: Logically connected; it comes from cohaerere, to stick together, so it shares the sticking root with adherent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「连贯的」，来自 cohaerere「粘在一起」，与 adherent 共享「黏住」词根。

entries.definition: A person who helps or backs a cause; broader than adherent and less tied to loyalty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支持者」，范围比 adherent 宽，与忠诚的绑定较弱。

entries.definition: A person who follows a leader or idea; it stresses following, not sticking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「追随者」，强调「跟随」而不是「黏附」。

entries.definition: A devoted follower of a teacher, especially religious; more personal and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门徒」，尤指宗教导师的忠实追随者，更个人化也更正式。

entries.definition: An enthusiastic follower of a person, activity or faith.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「热衷者、信徒」，指对某人、某活动或某信仰充满热情的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real haerere root and the political, religious and laboratory phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 haerere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的政治、宗教与实验室搭配。

normal.en: Adhaerere is ad plus haerere, to stick to; an adherent is one who sticks.
normal.cn: adhaerere 是 ad 加 haerere「黏住」，adherent 就是黏住的人。

normal.en: Adhesion is the physical force; adherence is the act or habit of sticking.
normal.cn: adhesion 是物理上的附着力；adherence 是黏附的动作或习惯。

normal.en: Adhesive is the substance that makes things stick.
normal.cn: adhesive 是让东西粘住的物质。

normal.en: An adherent of a policy keeps close to it and does not peel away.
normal.cn: 政策的 adherent 紧紧贴着它，不会脱落。

normal.en: Adherent cells must attach to a surface before they can grow.
normal.cn: 贴壁细胞必须先附着在表面才能生长。

abstract.en: Picture a label on glass that stays through every wash, still legible.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃上的标签经过每次冲洗都还在，字迹仍然清楚。

abstract.en: The same stickiness explains loyalty: a person held to an idea by conviction.
abstract.cn: 同一种「黏性」解释了忠诚：一个人被信念粘在一个理念上。

abstract.en: An adherent does not stand near a cause; they are attached to it and move with it.
abstract.cn: 拥护者不是站在事业旁边，而是附着于它并随它移动。

examples.en: The reform attracted adherents from both parties.
examples.cn: 这项改革吸引了两党的拥护者。

examples.en: An adherent coating must survive heat and moisture.
examples.cn: 附着涂层必须经受高温与潮湿。

examples.en: The scientist cultured adherent cells on a treated dish.
examples.cn: 科学家在处理过的培养皿上培养贴壁细胞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿希伦特」——阿希把标签贴在瓶上，冲了十次还粘着：拥护者、黏附的

root: 拉丁语 haerere「黏住」加 ad- 构成 adhaerere「黏附于」，现在分词 adhaerens 意为「黏着的」，经古法语进入英语为 adherent。haerere 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe something or someone that stays attached: to a cause, a faith, a surface, a dish, a rule, a party, a joint, or a substrate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「保持附着」的人或物：附着于事业、信仰、表面、培养皿、规则、政党、接头或基底。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label stays stuck to glass and will not peel off.
core.cn: 核心意象：标签牢牢粘在玻璃上，怎么也不脱落。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: a person stays attached to a movement or party.
branches.cn: 事业线：一个人黏附于某项运动或政党。

branches.en: THE BELIEF: faith and rules are held fast, not lightly followed.
branches.cn: 信念线：信仰与规则被紧紧抓住，而非轻率跟随。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BOND: a film, joint or layer remains attached.
branches.cn: 物理结合线：薄膜、接头或层保持附着。

branches.en: THE CELL: biology uses the same word for cells that must stick to a dish.
branches.cn: 细胞线：生物学用同一个词指必须贴住培养皿的细胞。

branches.en: THE PERSON: supporter and believer are both named by the sticking image.
branches.cn: 人物线：支持者与信徒都由「黏住」的画面来命名。

intro.en: Adherent is a Latin prefix plus a sticking root, shaped into a present participle and carried into English through French.
intro.cn: adherent 是拉丁语前缀加「黏住」词根，构成现在分词，再经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin haerere, adhaerere and adhaerens are recorded; haesum supplies the participle stem behind adhesion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 haerere、adhaerere、adhaerens 均有记录；haesum 提供 adhesion 背后的分词词干。

items.example: It directs the sticking toward a surface.
items.exampleCN: 它把「黏附」指向某个表面。

items.example: It is the sticking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「黏住」词根。

items.example: It joins the prefix and the root.

items.meaning: tending to, or a thing that

items.example: It forms cohesion, a related sticking-together term.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 cohesion，一个相关的「粘在一起」术语。
