definition_zh: 定期地；周期性地；间歇地；按期地；定时地；有规律地；按周期回归地；一阵一阵地；循环往复地
definition_en: at intervals that repeat, whether fixed by a schedule, by a natural cycle, or by an irregular rhythm that keeps coming back
core_image: 钟摆每次摆到同一个位置时发出的那一下轻响
scene: 机房的管理员把备份任务设成每隔十二小时自动运行一次。 The backup job runs periodically, every twelve hours.
sceneCN: 这里 periodically 是「定时地」（第 5 个义项：由设备按设定时间自动重复执行）；句意：备份任务定时运行，每十二小时一次。

pos.zh: 定期地；周期性地；间歇地

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: At planned intervals
senses.definition: at intervals set in advance by a plan, schedule, or rule, so that the action is repeated on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按计划、日程或规则预先设定的间隔进行，使该行为被有意重复
senses.example: The committee meets periodically to review the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会定期开会复核预算。
senses.why: The adverb is the adjective turned into a rhythm. Where periodic names the return, periodically names the manner of returning: the same step, repeated on a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 副词是把形容词变成一种节律。periodic 命名“回来”，periodically 命名“以回来的方式”：同样的步子，按日历重复。

senses.title: By a natural cycle
senses.definition: according to a cycle in nature, such as tides, seasons, or orbits, rather than a human schedule
senses.definitionCN: 依照自然界的循环，如潮汐、季节或轨道，而不是人为日程
senses.example: The lake level rises periodically with the monsoon.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水水位随季风周期性上升。
senses.why: Here the clock is not on a wall. The pendulum is the planet or the season, and periodically marks the return that no one arranged.
senses.whyCN: 这里的钟不挂在墙上。钟摆是行星或季节，periodically 标记的是无人安排却仍然发生的回归。

senses.title: In waves, with quiet gaps
senses.titleCN: 一阵一阵、中间有间歇地
senses.definition: in bursts that come and go, with quiet intervals between them, often without an exact schedule
senses.definitionCN: 以来了又去的一阵阵方式出现，之间隔着平静的间隔，常无精确日程
senses.example: The old radio periodically crackles for no clear reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧收音机会时不时地无故发出噼啪声。
senses.why: The return does not have to be exact to count. This sense loosens the interval and keeps only the image of something coming back in waves.
senses.whyCN: 回归不必精确也算数。这个义项放宽了间隔，只保留“某物一波一波回来”的意象。

senses.title: On a publication schedule
senses.definition: at the intervals at which a journal, magazine, or report is issued
senses.definitionCN: 按期刊、杂志或报告发行的间隔进行
senses.example: The survey is published periodically, usually in spring and autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这份调查定期发布，通常在春季和秋季。
senses.why: Publishing gave the word one of its oldest homes: an issue appears, disappears, and appears again. The period between issues is the interval the adverb names.
senses.whyCN: 出版业给了这个词最古老的落脚点之一：一期出现、消失、再出现。两期之间的那段时间就是副词命名的间隔。

senses.title: On an automatic timer
senses.definition: at intervals triggered automatically by a device, program, or timer rather than by a person
senses.definitionCN: 由设备、程序或计时器自动触发，而不是由人触发
senses.example: The sensor periodically uploads its readings to the server.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器定时把读数上传到服务器。
senses.why: A timer is a pendulum without a pendulum: it counts equal steps and fires. Here periodically describes machine rhythm, the most literal survival of the clock image.
senses.whyCN: 计时器是没有摆锤的钟摆：它数着相等的步子然后触发。这里的 periodically 描述机器节律，是钟表意象最字面的存留。

senses.title: As routine review or care
senses.titleCN: 作为例行复查或保养地
senses.definition: at regular intervals as part of health checks, maintenance, or quality control
senses.definitionCN: 作为健康检查、维护或质量控制的一部分，按固定间隔进行
senses.example: Patients on the drug are monitored periodically for liver function.
senses.exampleCN: 服用该药的患者会定期接受肝功能监测。
senses.why: Routine is a promise that someone will look again. The adverb turns care into a rhythm, so that neglect cannot quietly accumulate between visits.
senses.whyCN: 例行工作是一个承诺：还会有人再看一次。这个副词把照护变成节律，使疏忽无法在两次检查之间悄悄堆积。

senses.title: As a predicted return in the sky
senses.titleCN: 按可预测的天文周期地
senses.definition: at intervals fixed by an orbit, so that the return can be calculated years in advance
senses.definitionCN: 按轨道固定的间隔出现，使回归可以提前多年计算出来
senses.example: The comet passes periodically through the inner solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗彗星周期性地穿过内太阳系。
senses.why: Astronomy is where the word earned its trust: a return that can be written down before it happens. The adverb here is almost a mathematical guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 天文学是这个词赢得信任的地方：回归可以在发生之前就被写下来。这里的副词几乎等于一个数学保证。

senses.title: In cycles of boom and bust
senses.titleCN: 以繁荣与衰退的循环方式
senses.definition: in recurring phases of growth and decline, as in markets, epidemics, or public attention
senses.definitionCN: 以增长与衰退反复交替的阶段出现，如市场、疫情或公众注意力
senses.example: Housing starts periodically overshoot and then collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 住房开工量周期性地冲高，随后崩塌。
senses.why: The cycle is now made of human decisions rather than orbits. The adverb still marks a return, but the period is measured in confidence and credit rather than in degrees.
senses.whyCN: 这时的循环由人的决定构成，而不是轨道。副词仍标记回归，但周期用信心与信贷来度量，而不是用角度。

senses.title: Over and over, back to the same state
senses.definition: repeatedly, in a manner that returns to the same condition, used when the repetition itself is the point
senses.definitionCN: 反复进行并回到同一状态，用于强调重复本身即是重点
senses.example: The argument periodically resurfaces in different words.
senses.exampleCN: 这个争论会周期性地以不同说法重新浮出水面。
senses.why: The strongest form of the image: not just many times, but back to the same place. The adverb says the system has a resting point it cannot leave for good.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个意象最强的形式：不只是很多次，而是回到同一个地方。副词表示这个系统有一个它永远无法彻底离开的停留点。

intro.en: Periodically is periodic plus -ally, the regular English adverb ending built from -al and -ly. Periodic is Greek periodikos, from periodos 'a going around', built on peri- 'around' and hodos 'way'. The adverb simply carries the Greek image into the manner of an action: it tells you that something comes back the way a pendulum does.
intro.cn: periodically 是 periodic 加 -ally，即由 -al 与 -ly 构成的规则英语副词词尾。periodic 是希腊语 periodikos，出自 periodos“绕行一圈”，由 peri-“绕”与 hodos“路”构成。这个副词只是把希腊意象带进行为方式里：它告诉你某事像钟摆一样回来。

items.en: Hodos is 'way, road'; periodos is a going around. The adjective periodikos describes whatever belongs to such a circuit.
items.cn: hodos 是“路、道路”；periodos 是绕行一圈。形容词 periodikos 描述属于这种循环的一切。

items.en: English periodic appears for fevers and orbits that return at set intervals; the adverb follows the adjective as soon as writers need to say how an action recurs.
items.cn: 英语 periodic 先用于按固定间隔回归的发热与轨道；一旦作者需要说明行为如何重现，副词就随形容词出现。

items.en: Periodically settles into the language of administration, science, and publishing: reports issued periodically, instruments checked periodically.
items.cn: periodically 在 18 至 19 世纪进入行政、科学与出版语言：定期发布的报告、定期检查的仪器。

items.en: The ending is transparent: periodic → periodical (adjective) → periodically (adverb), or periodic + -ally. No meaning is added beyond 'in this manner'.
items.cn: 词尾是透明的：periodic → periodical（形容词）→ periodically（副词），或直接 periodic + -ally。除了“以这种方式”，没有增加任何意义。

items.en: Computing makes the adverb routine: processes that run periodically, backups taken periodically, jobs scheduled periodically.
items.cn: 计算机让这个副词成为日常用语：周期性运行的进程、定期执行的备份、定时调度的任务。

items.en: Periodontal begins with the same peri- but continues with odont- 'tooth'; it has nothing to do with intervals. The shared prefix is not a family relation.
items.cn: periodontal 以同一个 peri- 开头，但后面接的是 odont-“牙”，与间隔毫无关系。共享前缀并不是亲缘关系。

note.en: The first group separates the adverb from the adjective, the publication noun, and the base noun. The second group compares regular, intermittent, sporadic, and occasional timing.
note.cn: 第一组把副词与形容词、刊物名词、基础名词分开。第二组比较“规律地”“间歇地”“零星地”“偶尔地”四种时间方式。

entries.definition: recurring at equal intervals. The adverb adds only manner: happening in that recurring way.
entries.definitionCN: 以相等间隔重现的。副词只增加方式：以那种重现的方式发生。

entries.definition: a magazine or journal issued at regular intervals. As a noun it names a thing, not a manner of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔发行的杂志或期刊。作名词时它命名事物，而不是行为方式。

entries.definition: a length of time, a cycle, or a full stop. The adverb is built on the adjective of its cycle sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间、一个周期或一个句号。副词建在其周期义的形容词之上。

entries.definition: relating to the tissue around the teeth. Only the prefix matches; the root is odont- 'tooth'.
entries.definitionCN: 与牙周组织有关的。只有前缀相同，词根是 odont-“牙”。

entries.definition: at even, predictable intervals. It is the broadest word for steady timing; periodically adds the image of a full cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 以均匀、可预测的间隔。它是表示稳定时间的最宽泛的词；periodically 多了“完整一圈”的意象。

entries.definition: in a way that stops and starts. It lacks the regularity that periodically usually implies.
entries.definitionCN: 以时断时续的方式。它缺少 periodically 通常暗示的规律性。

entries.definition: at scattered, unpredictable moments. It is the opposite of a schedule, while periodically suggests at least a loose rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 在零散、不可预测的时刻。它与日程相反，而 periodically 至少暗示一种宽松的节律。

entries.definition: from time to time, without any pattern. It says the frequency is low and says nothing about intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 有时、偶尔，没有规律。它说明频率低，却不对间隔作任何说明。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: peri- 'around', hodos 'way', the -al/-ly adverb chain, the publishing and computing homes of the word, and the odont- trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：peri-“绕”、hodos“路”、-al/-ly 副词链、这个词在出版与计算机领域的落脚点，以及 odont- 陷阱。

normal.en: Periodos is a going around; periodically says an action takes that road again and again.
normal.cn: periodos 是绕行一圈；periodically 表示一个行为一次次走那条路。

normal.en: The ending is just -al plus -ly: periodic makes the adjective, and -ally makes the adverb without adding meaning.
normal.cn: 词尾只是 -al 加 -ly：periodic 构成形容词，-ally 构成副词，不增加意义。

normal.en: Publishing gave it 'issued periodically'; computing gave it 'runs periodically' — two homes of the same pendulum.
normal.cn: 出版业给了它“定期发行”，计算机给了它“定期运行”——同一个钟摆的两个落脚点。

normal.en: Regularly is about even spacing; periodically is about coming back around, which is why a cycle can be mentioned.
normal.cn: regularly 讲间隔均匀；periodically 讲绕回来，所以它才能带上“一个周期”。

normal.en: Periodontal has peri- but not hodos: teeth, not time.
normal.cn: periodontal 有 peri- 却没有 hodos：是牙，不是时间。

abstract.en: A metronome does not care whether anyone is listening; it keeps marking the same interval.
abstract.cn: 节拍器不在乎有没有人在听；它一直标着同样的间隔。

abstract.en: The tide comes back whether the harbour is ready or not, which is what makes a schedule a comfort.
abstract.cn: 不管港口准备好没有，潮水都会回来，这正是日程让人安心的原因。

abstract.en: A machine that checks itself periodically is a machine that has learned to distrust its own last answer.
abstract.cn: 会定期自检的机器，是一台学会了不信任自己上一个答案的机器。

examples.en: The files are backed up periodically to an off-site server.
examples.cn: 文件会定期备份到异地服务器。

examples.en: She checks the greenhouse periodically during cold spells.
examples.cn: 寒潮期间她会不时检查温室。

examples.en: The journal appears periodically, twice a year.
examples.cn: 这份期刊定期出版，每年两期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮瑞奥迪克利」——皮瑞围着操场一圈圈跑，每到同一个点就“滴”一声打卡 → periodically 定期地；周期性地（只借音，不表词源）

root: 希腊 periodos「绕行一圈」，由 peri-「绕」+ hodos「路」构成，形容词 periodikos，英语作 periodic；副词后缀 -ally（-al + -ly）。核心是「钟摆每次摆到同一点的那一下轻响」。periodontal（peri- + odont-「牙」）只是共享前缀，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of periodically all describe an action that comes back on a rhythm. What changes is who keeps the rhythm: a committee, a season, a faulty radio, a publisher, a timer, a clinic, an orbit, a market, or an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: periodically 的九个义项都描述一个按节律回来的行为。变化的是谁在维持节律：委员会、季节、坏收音机、出版方、计时器、诊所、轨道、市场，还是一个争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the small click a pendulum makes each time it returns to the same point.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟摆每次回到同一点时发出的那一下轻响。

branches.en: THE PLANNED CLICK: meetings, reviews, maintenance, and health checks set by people.
branches.cn: 计划好的那一下：由人设定的会议、复核、维护与健康检查。

branches.en: NATURE'S CLICK: seasons, tides, and orbits that return without a schedule.
branches.cn: 自然的那一下：没有日程却照样回归的季节、潮汐与轨道。

branches.en: THE LOOSE RHYTHM: bursts with quiet gaps, and repetition that keeps returning to the same state.
branches.cn: 宽松的节律：带平静间隔的一阵阵出现，以及不断回到同一状态的重复。

branches.en: THE PUBLISHED CLICK: issues that appear, vanish, and appear again.
branches.cn: 出版的那一下：出现、消失、再出现的期刊。

branches.en: MACHINE AND MARKET: timers firing automatically, and cycles of boom and bust.
branches.cn: 机器与市场：自动触发的计时器，以及繁荣与衰退的循环。

intro.en: Periodically is periodic + -ally, the standard English adverb ending. Periodic is Greek periodikos (periodos + -ikos). The word adds no new meaning; it moves the Greek image of a circuit into the manner of an action.
intro.cn: periodically 是 periodic 加 -ally，即标准英语副词词尾。periodic 是希腊语 periodikos（periodos + -ikos）。这个词不增加新意义，只是把希腊语“绕圈”的意象搬进行为方式。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root: periodos and periodikos are Greek. Latin only passed the forms periodus and periodicus into scientific prose, from which English took them.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词根：periodos 与 periodikos 都是希腊语。拉丁语只是把 periodus 与 periodicus 这两个形式传进科学散文，英语再从那里取用。

items.meaningCN: 以重复回归的方式；定期地（-ally 副词词尾）
属于循环的；周期性重现的
items.example: A periodic signal repeats its shape.
items.exampleCN: 周期信号会重复自己的形状。

items.meaning: a cycle, an interval, a full stop
items.example: The period of the orbit is 76 years.
items.exampleCN: 这条轨道的周期是七十六年。

items.meaningCN: 按间隔出版的刊物；期刊
items.example: The reading room keeps the periodicals on open shelves.
items.exampleCN: 阅览室把期刊放在开架上。

items.meaningCN: 重复回归的属性；周期性
items.example: Researchers measured the periodicity of the rainfall.
items.exampleCN: 研究者测量了降雨的周期性。

items.meaningCN: 不按固定间隔重现的；非周期的
items.example: The aperiodic signal is harder to predict.
The hodos in period once meant the road of a journey.
items.exampleCN: “时期”一词里的 hodos 曾指一段行程所走的路。

items.example: Peri- marks words that mean a circuit, such as a perimeter.
items.exampleCN: peri- 标记表示环行一周的词，例如表示“周长”的词。

items.meaningCN: 牙周的（peri- 绕 + odont- 牙）
items.exampleCN: 牙周护理能防止牙龈流失。

definition_zh: 供应链；供应链体系
definition_en: the whole sequence of suppliers, transport, storage and sellers that brings a product from raw material to the user
core_image: 货轮卸下零件，卡车送进仓库，最后由快递把包裹放到买家门口
scene: 货轮把零件运到港口，卡车再送进仓库，最后由快递送到买家门口。 The supply chain broke at the port, and every factory downstream idled for a week.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「从原料到用户之间的整条供应与流转链条」（第 1 个义项：把供应、运输、仓储与销售串起来的整体序列）；句意为港口那一环断了，下游每家工厂都停了一周。图中可辨识物件：货轮、港口吊机、卡车、仓库、快递包裹。

senses.title: The whole path from material to user
senses.titleCN: 从原料到用户的整条路径
senses.definition: every step, firm and movement that a product passes through before it reaches the buyer
senses.definitionCN: 产品到达买家之前所经过的每一步、每一家企业和每一次运输
senses.example: The supply chain broke at the port, and every factory downstream idled for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 港口那一环断了，下游每家工厂都停了一周。
senses.why: Supply is what is provided and a chain is links joined in order, so the phrase names the whole ordered path of provision.
senses.whyCN: 前一个词指被提供之物，后一个词指按顺序相接的环节，因此这个短语指供应的整条有序路径。

senses.title: One product's network of firms
senses.definition: the particular set of suppliers and carriers that serves one product line
senses.definitionCN: 为某一条产品线服务的那一组供应商与承运方
senses.example: Each model has its own supply chain of two hundred suppliers.
senses.exampleCN: 每个型号都有自己的供应链，涉及两百个供应商。
senses.why: Different products use different links, so the same phrase can name a specific network rather than the general idea.
senses.whyCN: 不同产品使用不同环节，因此同一短语也可以指一个具体网络，而非泛泛的概念。

senses.title: The management function
senses.definition: the business function that plans and controls these flows
senses.definitionCN: 规划与控制这些流动的商业职能
senses.example: The firm treats supply chain as a function, not a cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把供应链当作一项职能，而不是一项成本。
senses.why: A function is named after the flow it plans, so the people who arrange provision are said to run the supply chain.
senses.whyCN: 职能以它所规划的流动命名，因此安排供给的人被说成在管供应链。

senses.title: The upstream end
senses.definition: the part of the path nearest the raw materials, where risk often hides
senses.definitionCN: 路径中最靠近原料的那一段，风险常藏在这里
senses.example: The weakest link sits at the far end of the supply chain.
senses.exampleCN: 最弱的一环位于供应链的最远端。
senses.why: A chain has ends, and the end nearest extraction is called upstream because goods flow down from it.
senses.whyCN: 链条有两端，最靠近采掘的那一端因为货物流向下方而被称为上游。

senses.title: The risk of interruption
senses.definition: the exposure of this path to a failure at any one link
senses.definitionCN: 这条路径因任一环节失效而承受的风险
senses.example: Banks now ask how the supply chain would survive a flood.
senses.exampleCN: 银行现在会问，这条供应链在洪水中能否撑住。
senses.why: Once a path can be broken, the path itself becomes the thing exposed, so the phrase names the risk rather than the route.
senses.whyCN: 一条路径一旦可能断裂，路径本身就成了暴露在风险中的东西，因此该短语指风险而非路线。

senses.title: A short, local path
senses.definition: a deliberately shortened path, often regional, that reduces dependence on distant links
senses.definitionCN: 有意缩短、常为区域性的路径，以减少对远方环节的依赖
senses.example: The region rebuilt a short supply chain for vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区为蔬菜重建了一条短供应链。
senses.why: If distance is the problem, shortening the path is the remedy, and the phrase takes the adjective short.
senses.whyCN: 若距离是问题，缩短路径就是办法，这个短语便带上「短」的修饰。

senses.title: The tracked, visible path
senses.definition: the same path made visible from origin to shelf by tags and data
senses.definitionCN: 借助标签与数据，把从产地到货架的同一路径变得可见
senses.example: Tracking tags make the supply chain visible from ore to shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 追踪标签让供应链从矿石到货架都可见。
senses.why: A path you cannot see cannot be managed, so visibility became a property of the chain itself.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的路径无法管理，因此「可见」成了链条本身的一种属性。

senses.title: A path shared between rivals
senses.definition: a path in which competing firms use the same suppliers or carriers
senses.definitionCN: 竞争企业共用同一批供应商或承运方的路径
senses.example: Two rivals share one supply chain for batteries.
senses.exampleCN: 两家竞争对手共用一条电池供应链。
senses.why: When the same links serve different brands, the chain belongs to no single firm, which is the collaborative sense.
senses.whyCN: 当同一批环节服务不同品牌时，链条不属于任何一家企业，这就是协作义。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin verb of filling up from below with a Latin noun for a linked series. Both halves are old words; the pair is a twentieth-century business term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语中表示「从下面补足」的动词与表示「相连序列」的名词连在一起。两半都是古老的词，合起来则是二十世纪的商业术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Plere meant 'to fill'. Its pre-Latin root is reconstructed, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: plere 意为「填满」。其在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式，故来源不确定。

items.en: Sub- 'from below' plus plere 'fill' gave supplere, 'to fill up, to make complete, to furnish what is lacking'.
items.cn: sub-「从下面」加 plere「填满」构成 supplere，意为「补足、使完整、提供所缺之物」。

items.en: Catena meant 'a chain'. Its own origin is not settled; the link to any Indo-European root is a reconstruction, so source uncertain.
items.cn: catena 意为「链条」。其自身来源没有定论；与任何印欧词根的联系都属重构，故来源不确定。

items.en: Old French chaine carried the noun into English, where a chain is a series of linked parts or shops.
items.cn: 古法语 chaine 把这个名词带入英语，chain 指一串相连的环节或店铺。

items.en: Business writing of the later twentieth century joined the two nouns to describe the whole path of provision, and the term then spread to risk, finance and traceability.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的商业写作把这两个名词连用，描述供应的整条路径，此后该术语扩及风险、金融与可追踪性。

note.en: Group one holds compounds that also describe a linked path of business activity; group two holds words for the parts of that path.
note.cn: 第一组是同样描述商业活动链条的复合词；第二组是表示这条路径各环节的词。

entries.definition: The sequence of steps in which worth is added to a product; it follows money rather than goods.
entries.definitionCN: 指产品被逐步增值的序列，跟随的是钱而不是货。

entries.definition: The same path described from the customer's order backwards to the supplier.
entries.definitionCN: 同一条路径，从客户订单往回描述到供应商。

entries.definition: A web of suppliers rather than a single line, used when firms buy from many directions.
entries.definitionCN: 指网状的多向供应关系，用于企业从多个方向采购的情形。

entries.definition: Relating to production and incentives to produce; it is a policy term, not a physical path.
entries.definitionCN: 指生产及生产激励，是政策术语，不是实物路径。

entries.definition: The transport, storage and scheduling that carries goods along the chain.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿链条搬运货物的运输、仓储与调度。

entries.definition: The act of obtaining goods and services, one function inside the chain.
entries.definitionCN: 指获取商品与服务的行为，是链条内的一项职能。

entries.definition: The part that moves finished goods to shops and buyers.
entries.definitionCN: 指把成品送到店铺与买家的那一段。

entries.definition: The search for and choice of suppliers, which fixes the shape of the chain.
entries.definitionCN: 指寻找并选定供应商，决定了链条的形状。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first noun means filling up what is lacking; the second means a series of links.
normal.cn: 前一个名词指补足所缺，后一个名词指一串相接的环节。

normal.en: The family runs supply, supplier, sourcing and the verb for providing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括供应、供应商、寻源，以及表示提供的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: management, disruption, risk, visibility, upstream.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：供应链管理、供应链中断、供应链风险、供应链可视化、上游。

normal.en: A chain is only as strong as its weakest link, which is why the word is used for risk.
normal.cn: 链条的强度取决于最弱的一环，因此这个词常与风险连用。

normal.en: The phrase can mean the general idea, one product's network, or a single firm's function.
normal.cn: 这个短语可以指一般概念、某一产品的网络，或某家公司的职能。

abstract.en: Picture a single parcel that has passed through six pairs of hands before reaching a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包裹在到达一扇门之前经过了六双手。

abstract.en: Picture one broken link and a whole line of machines standing still.
abstract.cn: 想象一个环节断掉，整排机器静止不动。

abstract.en: Picture two competing badges fed by the same conveyor.
abstract.cn: 想象两个互相竞争的商标由同一条传送带供料。

examples.en: The report maps the supply chain from mine to shop.
examples.cn: 报告把从矿场到商店的供应链画了出来。

examples.en: A longer supply chain means more places where it can fail.
examples.cn: 供应链越长，可能出问题的地方就越多。

examples.en: They shortened the supply chain by buying from nearby farms.
examples.cn: 他们向附近农场采购，缩短了供应链。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「supply（供应）+ chain（链条）」——一环扣一环的供应路径 → 供应链

root: 英语复合短语：前半底子是拉丁语「从下面补足」的动词，由意为「从下面」的前缀与「填满」动词构成；后半底子是拉丁语「链条」名词，其自身来源无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one path: the whole route from material to buyer, one product's own network, the office that manages it, its upstream end, its exposure to failure, a deliberately short version, a tracked version, and a version shared by rivals.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条路径展开：从原料到买家的整条路线、某一产品自己的网络、管理它的部门、它的上游一端、它面对的中断风险、有意缩短的版本、可追踪的版本，以及被竞争对手共用的版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a container unloaded at a quay, carried by lorry to a warehouse, then handed to a courier at a front door.
core.cn: 核心意象：集装箱在码头卸下，由卡车送到仓库，最后在前门交给快递员。

branches.en: THE WHOLE ROUTE: the phrase's basic sense is the complete path from extraction to the buyer.
branches.cn: 整条路线：这个短语的基本义就是从采掘到买家的完整路径。

branches.en: A NETWORK WITH ENDS: one product's set of suppliers has an upstream end where risk concentrates.
branches.cn: 有端点的网络：某一产品的供应商集合有一个风险集中的上游端点。

branches.en: WHO OWNS THE PATH: a managed function belongs to one firm, while a shared chain belongs to none.
branches.cn: 谁拥有路径：被管理的职能属于一家企业，而被共用的链条不属于任何一家。

branches.en: SEEING THE RISK: exposure to failure and tracking from ore to shelf are the same concern, one before and one after the break.
branches.cn: 看见风险：中断风险与从矿石到货架的可追踪，是同一份担忧，一个在断裂前，一个在断裂后。

branches.en: SHORTENING: a local path is the same chain with fewer links.
branches.cn: 缩短：本地路径就是环节更少的同一条链条。

intro.en: The phrase is two Latin-rooted nouns: one for filling a lack, one for a series of links, which together describe provision as a path.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁词根的名词构成：一个表示「补足所缺」，一个表示「一串环节」，合起来把供应描述成一条路径。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplere gives supply, supplier and supplement; Latin catena gives chain and the idea of linked series.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「补足」的动词衍生出供应、供应商与补充物；拉丁语表示「链条」的名词衍生出链条以及「相连序列」的观念。

items.example: The prefix places the filling beneath the lack.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「填补」放在缺口的下方。

items.structure: plere, plevi, pletum (Latin verb, second conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the idea of completing a shortage.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「补足短缺」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole first noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是前半名词的来源。

items.example: The noun and verb both name provision.
The noun supplies the image of links in order.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「环节按序相接」的意象。

items.example: The word covers metal links and linked shops alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词兼指金属链环与连锁店铺。

items.example: The agent suffix names the firm at the start of a link.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指链条起点处的企业。

items.example: The compound is a twentieth-century business term.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是二十世纪的商业术语。

definition_zh: 主要地；首要地；大体上
definition_en: chiefly, above all other things or in the leading position
core_image: 一张圆桌上只有一个座位摆在正中，其余都在侧边
scene: 这家小公司做的是沿海运输，别的业务只是顺便。 The small firm is principally engaged in coastal shipping.
sceneCN: 这里指正式文体中的主营活动（第 8 个义项：法律或金融文本中的「主要从事」）；句意为这家小公司主要从事沿海航运。

senses.title: Chiefly
senses.definition: for the most part, above all other things
senses.definitionCN: 大部分情况下，超过其他一切
senses.example: The region is principally agricultural.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区主要务农。
senses.why: The word ranks one activity above others, close to chiefly but heavier in tone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把某项活动排在其余之上，接近「主要地」，但语气更重。

senses.title: First in importance
senses.definition: used of what matters most in a hierarchy
senses.definitionCN: 用于等级体系中最重要的事物
senses.example: The fund is principally for research, not buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔基金主要用于研究，而不是建筑。
senses.why: Here the word ranks importance rather than quantity, often in institutional decisions.
senses.whyCN: 这里它排的是重要性而非数量，常见于机构决策。

senses.title: Principally because
senses.definition: used to name the dominant cause
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出主导原因
senses.example: The delay was principally due to a shortage of funds.
senses.exampleCN: 延误主要是资金短缺造成的。
senses.why: The causal pattern selects the leading reason and lets others remain in the background.
senses.whyCN: 这一因果句式挑出主导理由，让其他理由留在背景。

senses.title: Principally responsible for
senses.definition: used of the agent with the leading duty
senses.definitionCN: 用于承担首要职责的主体
senses.example: The ministry is principally responsible for the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 该部门对这项政策负主要责任。
senses.why: The phrase assigns responsibility at the top of an institutional chain.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语把责任放在机构链条的最上层。

senses.title: Principally concerned with
senses.definition: used of a text or field focused on one question
senses.definitionCN: 指文本或领域聚焦于某一问题
senses.example: The chapter is principally concerned with property rights.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章主要涉及财产权。
senses.why: Academic summaries use the phrase to state the centre of a discussion.
senses.whyCN: 学术摘要用这一短语说明讨论的中心。

senses.title: Principally used for
senses.definition: of a place or object, serving one main function
senses.definitionCN: 指场所或物品承担一项主要功能
senses.example: The hall is principally used for concerts.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅主要用于音乐会。
senses.why: The pattern states the main function and leaves other uses as exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式说明主要功能，把其他用途留作例外。

senses.title: Principally aimed at
senses.definition: of a measure, intended to affect one group or problem
senses.definitionCN: 指措施意在影响某一群体或问题
senses.example: The tax is principally aimed at large estates.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税主要针对大型地产。
senses.why: Policy writing uses the word to identify the main target of an instrument.
senses.whyCN: 政策写作借此词指出一项工具的主要目标。

senses.title: Formal and legal main activity
senses.definition: in legal or financial prose, describing the main business of a company
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或金融文字中描述公司的主要业务
senses.example: The company is principally engaged in coastal shipping.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司主要从事沿海航运。
senses.why: The fixed legal phrase marks the core activity, a use where the word's formality is strongest.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定法律短语标记核心业务，是这个词正式感最强的用法。

intro.en: Principally comes from the Latin adjective for belonging to the chief, built on the words for first and take, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「属于首领的」形容词，其词根由「第一」与「拿取」构成，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adjective primus means first.
items.cn: 形容词意为「第一的」。

items.en: The verb capere means to take or seize.
items.cn: 动词意为「拿取、抓取」。

items.en: The noun princeps, first taker, means the leading person; its stem princip- supplies the adjective.
items.cn: 名词字面「首先拿取者」，指首领；其词干提供形容词。

items.en: The adjective principalis means belonging to the chief or first rank.
items.cn: 形容词意为「属于首领或首位的」。

items.en: English principal comes through French and means chief or main, as adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入，作形容词与名词都表「首要的、负责人」。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix and settles in formal, legal and financial prose; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀，定居于正式、法律与金融文体；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin chief-stem, including two words often confused; the second group contrasts leading rank with main importance or plain majority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「首领」词干，其中包括两个常被混淆的词；第二组对照「首领地位」与「主要重要性」或「单纯多数」。

entries.definition: Chief or main; also the head of a school or a sum of money.
entries.definitionCN: 首要的、主要的；也指校长或本金。

entries.definition: A rule or basic truth; it comes from the beginning-branch of the same stem, not from principal.
entries.definitionCN: 规则或基本原理；来自同一词干的「开端」分支，而非「首要的」那一支。

entries.definition: A royal son or ruler of a small state, from the same first-taker noun.
entries.definitionCN: 王子或小国统治者，来自同一个「首先拿取者」名词。

entries.definition: A small state ruled by a prince.
entries.definitionCN: 由亲王统治的小国；公国。

entries.definition: Above all others, with a neutral tone.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，语气中性。

entries.definition: For the most part; the plain everyday choice.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分情况下；日常最朴素的选择。

entries.definition: Mainly, with emphasis on first-order importance or purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地，强调第一序的重要性或目的。

entries.definition: More than everything else, with explicit ranking.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，带明确排序。

entries.definition: For the most part, allowing exceptions.
entries.definitionCN: 大体上，允许例外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real first-taker root and the real split between leading rank and plain majority.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「首先拿取者」词根，并区分「首领地位」与「单纯多数」。

normal.en: The root is first taker, so the word points to whoever or whatever stands at the head.
normal.cn: 词根是「首先拿取者」，所以这个词指向站在最前面的那个人或那件事。

normal.en: Principal and principle look identical but come from two branches: leader and beginning.
normal.cn: 「负责人」与「原理」拼写相同，却来自两条分支：首领与开端。

normal.en: Principally engaged in is the legal way to name a company's core business.
normal.cn: 「主要从事」是法律上命名公司核心业务的说法。

normal.en: Principally responsible puts the duty at the top of the chain.
normal.cn: 「负主要责任」把职责放在链条顶端。

normal.en: In formal prose it sounds heavier than mainly, which is the point.
normal.cn: 在正式散文里它比「主要地」更重，这正是它的用处。

abstract.en: A principal seat is central not because it is bigger, but because the table is arranged around it.
abstract.cn: 主位之所以居中，不是因为椅子更大，而是因为桌子围着它摆。

abstract.en: Leadership is a rank, while main importance is a weight; the word can lean either way.
abstract.cn: 首领是一种等级，主要性是一种分量；这个词两边都能靠。

abstract.en: Formality here is a way of making a ranking sound like a fact.
abstract.cn: 这里的正式感，是把排序说得像事实的一种方式。

examples.en: The island is principally known for its birds.
examples.cn: 这座岛主要以鸟类闻名。

examples.en: The scheme is principally funded by the central government.
examples.cn: 这项计划主要由中央政府出资。

examples.en: The chapter is principally about the early years of the project.
examples.cn: 这一章主要讲项目的早期年份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普林西普利」——首领坐正位，事情主要归他

root: 拉丁语「第一」与「拿取」合成名词「首先拿取者、首领」，其词干构成形容词「属于首领的」；英语经法语借入形容词「首要的」，再加副词后缀。「原理」一词来自同词干的另一分支「开端」，与本词同源不同义。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate chief activity, first importance, dominant cause, leading responsibility, academic focus, main function, policy target and the formal legal main business.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理主要活动、首要重要性、主导原因、首要责任、学术关注、主要功能、政策目标，以及正式法律文体中的主营。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round table with one seat at the centre and the rest along the side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张圆桌，只有一个座位在正中，其余都在侧边。

branches.en: THE HEAD PLACE: chief activity and first importance in a hierarchy.
branches.cn: 首位：主要活动与等级中的首要重要性。

branches.en: THE LEADING REASON AND DUTY: dominant cause and top responsibility.
branches.cn: 主导理由与职责：主导原因与最高责任。

branches.en: THE ACADEMIC CENTRE: the question a text is mainly about.
branches.cn: 学术中心：文本主要讨论的问题。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: main function and policy target.
branches.cn: 工具：主要功能与政策目标。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CORE BUSINESS: the legal phrase for a company's main activity.
branches.cn: 正式核心业务：用于公司主营的法律短语。

intro.en: Principally is a Latin first-word, a taking-root, a chief-noun, an adjective suffix and an English adverb suffix; the same stem also yields principle by a different branch.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「第一」、 「拿取」词根、表「首领」的名词、形容词后缀与英语副词后缀构成；同一词干经另一分支还产生「原理」。

latinIntro.en: The chief noun is literally first taker; its stem builds principal, while a beginning-branch builds principle.
latinIntro.cn: 表「首领」的名词字面是「首先拿取者」；其词干构成「首要的」，另一「开端」分支则构成「原理」。

items.example: The adjective supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供合成词的前半。

items.example: The verb supplies the taking half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供合成词中「拿取」的那一半。

items.example: The noun names the person at the head of a group.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指群体最前面的那个人。

items.example: The suffix turns the chief noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「首领」名词变成形容词。

items.example: The adjective ranks a thing by its leading position.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词按首领地位为事物排序。

definition_zh: 回归线；热带地区；（古）转折点
definition_en: either of the two parallels of latitude where the sun stands directly overhead at the solstice
core_image: 太阳在天空缓缓北移，到达一条界线后停住并折返，那条界线就是回归线
scene: 课本上的图示标出太阳直射点折返的那条界线。 The diagram marks the Tropic of Cancer, where the noon sun stands overhead in June and then turns back.
sceneCN: 这里 tropic 指「太阳在夏至正午直射并随后折返的纬线」（第 1 个义项：北回归线）；句意为示意图标出北回归线，六月正午太阳在此当顶，随后转向南移。图中可辨识物件：地球、太阳光线、回归线、箭头。

senses.title: The Tropic of Cancer
senses.titleCN: 北回归线：太阳北移的极限纬线
senses.definition: the northern parallel at about twenty-three and a half degrees north, where the sun is overhead at the June solstice
senses.definitionCN: 约北纬二十三度半、夏至时太阳直射的纬线
senses.example: The Tropic of Cancer crosses the Sahara and southern China.
senses.exampleCN: 北回归线穿过撒哈拉与中国南方。
senses.why: Greek trope 'a turn' names the line where the sun turns back; the northern one is named for the sign the sun entered.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 trope「转折」命名太阳折返之处；北面那条因太阳进入的星座而得名。

senses.title: The Tropic of Capricorn
senses.titleCN: 南回归线：太阳南移的极限纬线
senses.definition: the southern parallel at about twenty-three and a half degrees south, where the sun is overhead at the December solstice
senses.definitionCN: 约南纬二十三度半、冬至时太阳直射的纬线
senses.example: The Tropic of Capricorn runs through Australia and southern Africa.
senses.exampleCN: 南回归线穿过澳大利亚与非洲南部。
senses.why: The southern line is the same turn seen from the other hemisphere, named for the sign the sun enters in December.
senses.whyCN: 南面这条线是从另一半球看到的同一次折返，因太阳十二月进入的星座而得名。

senses.title: The tropics as a region
senses.titleCN: 热带地区：南北回归线之间的地带
senses.definition: the region of the earth between the two tropics
senses.definitionCN: 地球上两条回归线之间的地带
senses.example: Coffee and bananas grow throughout the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡与香蕉在整个热带地区都有种植。
senses.why: The two lines bound a belt, and the plural name of the lines became the name of the belt.
senses.whyCN: 两条线围出一条带，线的复数名称就成了这条带的名称。

senses.title: Tropical, as an attributive adjective
senses.titleCN: 热带的：作定语的形容词用法
senses.definition: relating to the tropics, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 与热带有关的，用于名词前
senses.example: Tropic heat and moisture favour dense forest.
senses.exampleCN: 热带的炎热与湿润有利于密林生长。
senses.why: English often uses the shorter tropic before a noun where tropical would also fit, a clipped attributive use.
senses.whyCN: 英语在名词前常用较短的 tropic，而 tropical 同样适用，这是截短的定语用法。

senses.title: The celestial tropic
senses.titleCN: 天球回归线：太阳在天球上的折返圈
senses.definition: either of the two circles on the celestial sphere marking the sun's greatest declination
senses.definitionCN: 天球上标出太阳最大赤纬的两条圈之一
senses.example: The celestial tropic touches the ecliptic at the solstice points.
senses.exampleCN: 天球回归线在二至点与黄道相切。
senses.why: The sky repeats the terrestrial limit in its own circles, marking where the sun's declination stops.
senses.whyCN: 天空用它自己的圈重复地表的界限，标出太阳赤纬停止之处。

senses.title: A turning point, archaic
senses.titleCN: 转折点：事情转向的时刻（古义）
senses.definition: a point of turning or change, the older general sense of the Greek root
senses.definitionCN: 转向或改变的时刻，即希腊词根的较早一般义
senses.example: The old text speaks of the tropic of fortune.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧文谈到命运的转折点。
senses.why: The root's general sense of turning survives in older writing about any change of course.
senses.whyCN: 词根的一般「转向」义在谈论任何路线改变的旧文字中留存。

senses.title: A tropic response in biology
senses.titleCN: 向性的：生物对刺激转向的反应
senses.definition: describing a movement or growth directed by a stimulus such as light or gravity
senses.definitionCN: 描述由光、重力等刺激引导的运动或生长
senses.example: Roots show a tropic response to gravity.
senses.exampleCN: 根对重力表现出向性反应。
senses.why: A plant organ turns toward or away from a stimulus, which is the root's literal 'turn' applied to growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物器官朝刺激转向或背离，正是词根字面的「转」用于生长。

senses.title: The torrid zone between the tropics
senses.titleCN: 热带地带：两回归线之间的气候带
senses.definition: the hot climate belt lying between the two tropics
senses.definitionCN: 位于两条回归线之间的炎热气候带
senses.example: The torrid zone receives the sun almost vertically all year.
senses.exampleCN: 热带地带全年几乎接受垂直照射的阳光。
senses.why: The belt between the lines stays hot because the sun remains high there throughout the year.
senses.whyCN: 两线之间的地带之所以炎热，是因为太阳全年都保持在较高位置。

intro.en: Tropic comes from Latin tropicus, from Greek tropikos 'of a turn, of the solstice', built on trope 'a turn' and trepein 'to turn'. The lines are named for the sun's turning at the solstices. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tropic 来自拉丁 tropicus，源于希腊 tropikos「转折的、至点的」，由 trope「转折」与 trepein「转动」构成；这两条线因太阳在二至点折返而得名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trope meant 'a turn, a turning', especially of the sun or of a argument.
items.cn: trope 意为「转折、转向」，尤指太阳的折返或论证的转折。

items.en: Trepein meant 'to turn'. The noun and verb form one of the most productive roots in Greek.
items.cn: trepein 意为「转动」。这个名词与动词构成希腊语中最多产的词根之一。

items.en: Tropikos meant 'of a turn', and in astronomy 'of the solstice', because the sun appears to turn back there.
items.cn: tropikos 意为「转折的」，在天文学中指「至点的」，因为太阳在那里看似折返。

items.en: Latin borrowed the adjective as tropicus; the noun tropicus circulus named the solstitial circle.
items.cn: 拉丁把这个形容词借作 tropicus；名词短语 tropicus circulus 指至点圈。

items.en: English tropic appears in the sixteenth century for the two solstitial parallels, and the plural tropics soon named the belt between them.
items.cn: 英语 tropic 在 16 世纪出现，指两条至点纬线；复数 the tropics 很快指它们之间的地带。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the biological 'tropic response' sense and the archaic 'turning point' sense have no precisely dated first English use; the Greek root is not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：生物学的「向性反应」义与古义「转折点」在英语中的确切首见年代未见记录；希腊词根则无争议。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound like tropic; group two holds the lines and belts it belongs to.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近 tropic 的词；第二组是它所归属的线与地带。

entries.definition: A subject of discussion, from Greek ta topika 'things about places'; it is not related to turning.
entries.definitionCN: 讨论的主题，来自希腊 ta topika「关于处所之事」；与「转动」无关。

entries.definition: A prize or memorial, from Greek tropaion 'a rout of the enemy'; the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 奖品或纪念物，来自希腊 tropaion「击溃敌人」；词根不同。

entries.definition: A directed growth response to a stimulus, built on the same Greek trope 'turn'.
entries.definitionCN: 对刺激的有方向生长反应，同出希腊 trope「转」。

entries.definition: A figurative turn of phrase, literally a 'turning' of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 比喻性的说法，字面就是意义的「转向」。

entries.definition: The zero-latitude circle halfway between the tropics, where day and night are equal.
entries.definitionCN: 两条回归线正中的零度纬线，那里昼夜等长。

entries.definition: Angular distance from the equator; the tropics are two particular latitudes.
entries.definitionCN: 相对赤道的角距离；回归线是两个特定的纬度。

entries.definition: Any circle parallel to the equator; a tropic is one named parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 与赤道平行的任一圈；回归线是其中有名的一条。

entries.definition: The two times of year when the sun reaches its greatest declination and turns back.
entries.definitionCN: 一年中太阳到达最大赤纬并折返的两个时刻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek 'turn', real solstice astronomy and real geography, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「转」、真实的至点天文与真实地理，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Trope 'a turn' + -ic: the line where the sun turns back at the solstice.
normal.cn: trope「转折」+ -ic：太阳在至点折返的那条线。

normal.en: The Tropic of Cancer is northern; the Tropic of Capricorn is southern.
normal.cn: 北回归线在北，南回归线在南。

normal.en: The tropics lie between the two tropics and are hot all year.
normal.cn: the tropics 位于两条回归线之间，全年炎热。

normal.en: The same Greek root gives tropism, a plant's turning response to light.
normal.cn: 同一希腊词根衍生 tropism，即植物对光的转向反应。

normal.en: Celestial tropics mark the sun's greatest declination on the sky.
normal.cn: 天球回归线标出太阳在天球上的最大赤纬。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum that swings north and stops just before returning.
abstract.cn: 想象一只向北摆动的摆锤，在返回前停住。

abstract.en: Picture a path with two marked fences, beyond which the sun never goes overhead.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路两侧各有一道标线，太阳从不越过它们当顶。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that changes direction at a single sharp word.
abstract.cn: 想象一场对话在一个尖刻的词上突然转向。

examples.en: The Tropic of Cancer passes through the northern hemisphere.
examples.cn: 北回归线穿过北半球。

examples.en: Rainforests cover much of the tropics.
examples.cn: 雨林覆盖了热带地区的大部分。

examples.en: The sun stands overhead at the tropic on the solstice.
examples.cn: 至点时太阳在回归线上当顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: trop（转，如 trope 转义）+ ic → 太阳折返的线 → 回归线、热带

root: 希腊 tropikos「转折的、至点的」= trope「转折」+ -ikos；源于 trepein「转动」，指太阳在二至点折返的纬线。拉丁 tropicus，英语 16 世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses revolve around one turn: the two solstitial parallels where the sun reverses, the belt they enclose, the attributive use, the sky's corresponding circles, the old 'turning point', the biological turning response, and the hot zone itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次「折返」：太阳转向的两条至点纬线、它们围出的地带、定语用法、天空中的对应圈、古义「转折点」、生物学的转向反应，以及炎热地带本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun moving north or south, reaching a marked line, and turning back.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳向北或向南移动，到达一条标线后折返。

branches.en: TWO LIMITS: the northern and southern parallels mark the two ends of the sun's yearly swing.
branches.cn: 两条界线：南北两条纬线标出太阳一年摆动的两端。

branches.en: THE BELT: the space between the lines becomes a hot region and a climate zone.
branches.cn: 地带：两线之间的空间成为炎热地区与气候带。

branches.en: ATTRIBUTIVE: the short form works before a noun as a clipped adjective.
branches.cn: 定语：较短形式可在名词前作截短形容词。

branches.en: SKY: the celestial tropics mirror the earthly limits on the celestial sphere.
branches.cn: 天空：天球回归线在天球上镜像地表的界限。

branches.en: TURNING: the old sense names any turning point, and biology names a growth response that turns toward a stimulus.
branches.cn: 转折：古义指任何转折点，生物学则指朝刺激转向的生长反应。

intro.en: Tropic is an adjective from Greek 'turn'; its family includes tropical, tropism and trope, all built on the same root.
intro.cn: tropic 是来自希腊「转」的形容词；其词族包括 tropical、tropism 与 trope，均建于同一词根。

latinIntro.en: Greek trope 'a turn' and trepein 'to turn' give tropikos, Latin tropicus and English tropic; the same root yields tropical and tropism, while trophy comes from a different Greek branch, tropaion 'a rout'.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 trope「转折」与 trepein「转动」衍生 tropikos、拉丁 tropicus 与英语 tropic；同一词根还衍生 tropical 与 tropism，而 trophy 来自另一支希腊词 tropaion「击溃」。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「转动」的动作。

items.example: A trope in rhetoric is a turn of meaning.
items.exampleCN: 修辞中的 trope 是意义的转向。

definition_zh: 提起诉讼；打官司；在法庭上争讼
definition_en: to bring a dispute before a court and argue it there
core_image: 把一场口角装进正式文书，送进法院的大门，然后在庭上逐条争辩
scene: 合同里写明，谈不拢就把争议交给法院，而不是私下和解。 Either party may litigate if mediation fails.
sceneCN: 这里 litigate 指把争议提交法院并通过诉讼解决（第 4 个义项：选择诉讼途径而非私下和解）；句意：若调解失败，任何一方都可以提起诉讼。图中可辨识物件：合同、法院大门、调解桌、双方席位。

senses.title: Take a dispute to court
senses.definition: to settle a disagreement by bringing it before a court

senses.example: The two families litigated for eleven years over the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 两家人为那片果园打了十一年官司。

senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 litigation 的动作版：制度用多年做的事，双方一旦选择就这么做。

senses.title: Sue a person or company
senses.titleCN: 对某人或某公司提起诉讼

senses.definitionCN: 针对特定对手提起案件
senses.example: They litigated the supplier rather than write off the loss.
senses.exampleCN: 他们选择起诉供应商，而不是把损失一笔勾销。
senses.why: Once the dispute has an opponent, the verb takes an object, because the action is aimed at someone rather than at a principle.
senses.whyCN: 争议一旦有了对手，这个动词就带宾语，因为动作指向某个人，而不是某个原则。

senses.title: Argue the points in court
senses.definition: to present and contest arguments before a judge
senses.definitionCN: 在法官面前陈述并辩驳各项主张
senses.example: Counsel litigated every clause of the lease line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 律师把租约的每一条逐行争辩了一遍。
senses.why: The 'driving' half of the Latin verb shows here: the case is pushed forward argument by argument, not decided in one gesture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词中「驱动」的那一半在这里显形：案子是一段论一段论地往前推，而不是一个动作就判完。

senses.title: Choose the court over a deal
senses.definition: to pursue a remedy through the courts instead of negotiating
senses.definitionCN: 通过法院寻求救济而不是谈判
senses.example: Either party may litigate if mediation fails.
senses.exampleCN: 若调解失败，任何一方都可以提起诉讼。
senses.why: Mediation asks the parties to agree; litigating hands the decision to a third party, so choosing the verb marks a refusal to compromise.
senses.whyCN: 调解要求双方同意；打官司则把决定交给第三方，所以选用这个动词就等于拒绝妥协。

senses.title: Carry a client's case
senses.definition: to conduct a case on behalf of a client, as a lawyer does
senses.definitionCN: 像律师那样代表当事人进行诉讼
senses.example: She has litigated patent cases for two decades.
senses.exampleCN: 她代理专利案件已有二十年。
senses.why: A profession can take the same verb because its daily work is exactly this act repeated for other people.
senses.whyCN: 一个行业可以采用同一个动词，因为它每天做的事正是替别人重复这个动作。

senses.title: Fight the same issue again
senses.definition: to reopen or repeat a contested issue in court
senses.definitionCN: 在法院重新开启或重复争辩同一争点
senses.example: The losing side tried to litigate the same question twice.
senses.exampleCN: 败诉方试图把同一个问题再打一次。
senses.why: Because courts keep a record, repetition becomes visible as a distinct act, and the language marks it with a prefix.
senses.whyCN: 因为法院留有记录，重复就成了一个可见的独立动作，语言便用前缀把它标出来。

senses.title: Push a cause through the courts
senses.titleCN: 借司法途径推进某项主张
senses.definition: to advance a broader cause by means of court cases
senses.definitionCN: 通过一系列案件推进更广泛的主张
senses.example: Advocates litigated until the polluting plant closed.
senses.exampleCN: 倡导者们一路打官司，直到那家污染工厂关闭。
senses.why: A single case is a tool, and a movement can use the verb for years of cases aimed at one social goal.
senses.whyCN: 单件案件是工具，一场运动可以用这个动词概括多年案件，指向同一个社会目标。

senses.title: Quarrel in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, simply to quarrel or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，泛指争吵、争辩
senses.example: The chronicle says the brothers litigated over the inheritance for a season.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史记载，兄弟俩为遗产争了一季。
senses.why: The Latin verb covered quarrelling before it narrowed to court business, and older English keeps that wider shade.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词在收窄为法院事务之前泛指争吵，较早的英语仍保留这层更宽的意思。

intro.en: Litigate comes straight from the past participle of Latin litigare 'to go to law'. The verb is transparent: lis 'dispute' plus agere 'to drive'. The deeper origin of lis is unsettled.
intro.cn: litigate 直接来自拉丁 litigare「诉诸法院」的过去分词。构词一目了然：lis「争执」加 agere「驱动」。lis 更深来源没有定论。

items.en: Lis (genitive litis) meant a quarrel or a lawsuit. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and the Indo-European forms occasionally proposed for it are reconstructions rather than established derivations.
items.cn: lis（属格 litis）指口角或诉讼。其更深来源属来源不确定，偶尔为它提出的印欧语形式只是重构，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Agere meant to drive or set in motion, and by extension to do, to plead, to carry on. It supplies the forward push in litigate and also stands behind act, agent and agenda.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、使运动，引申为做、陈述、推进。它在 litigate 中提供向前的推力，也是 act、agent、agenda 的来源。

items.en: Lis plus agere gave litigare, 'to dispute, to plead, to go to law', with the past participle litigatus. The word kept both the quarrel and the courtroom in one meaning.
items.cn: lis 加 agere 构成 litigare「争执、陈述、诉诸法院」，过去分词为 litigatus。这个词把口角与法庭放在同一个意思里。

items.en: English took the verb in the seventeenth century through legal writing, when cases were increasingly argued by trained counsel rather than by the parties in person.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪经法律文书借入这个动词，当时案件越来越多由受过训练的律师而非当事人本人辩论。

items.en: Modern English uses the verb for parties and for lawyers, and pairs it with abstract objects such as a claim, an issue or a clause; the old 'quarrel' sense survives only in historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它说当事人，也用它说律师，并可带请求、争点、条款等抽象宾语；古老的「争吵」义只留在历史文本里。

note.en: Group one holds the same lis stem and two near neighbours, one of which even shares the Latin verb of driving; group two holds the everyday synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 lis 的词干亲属，外加两个近邻词，其中一个甚至共享拉丁的「驱动」动词；第二组是日常同义词。

entries.definition: The activity or the whole proceeding; the verb names one act within it.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动或整套程序；动词则指其中的一个动作。

entries.definition: A party to a case, marked by the -ant suffix of the one acting.
entries.definitionCN: 案件当事方，带 -ant 后缀，表示正在行动的人。

entries.definition: Given to lawsuits; it describes a habit, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 爱打官司的；描述一种习惯，而不是一次动作。

entries.definition: To make less severe, from mitis 'mild' plus agere; it looks like litigate but the first element is not lis.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻、缓和，由 mitis「温和」加 agere 构成；外形像 litigate，第一个成分却不是 lis。

entries.definition: To make laws, from lex 'law' plus latio 'a bringing'; it is about writing rules, not arguing cases.
entries.definitionCN: 立法，由 lex「法律」加 latio「带来」构成；它关乎写规则，不是争案件。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for beginning a civil case; litigate also covers the arguing that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 启动民事案件的日常动词；litigate 还覆盖之后的争辩过程。

entries.definition: To pursue a criminal charge, usually as the state; it belongs to public law, while litigate belongs to private disputes.
entries.definitionCN: 追究刑事指控，通常由国家进行；它属公法，而 litigate 属私人争议。

entries.definition: To dispute or oppose a claim, in court or elsewhere; it says nothing about procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 对某项主张提出异议或反对，可在法院内外；它不涉及程序。

entries.definition: To argue that something is wrong, or the disagreement itself, before any court is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 指在法院介入之前就某事争辩，或指分歧本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real Latin pieces and the real derivative family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个真实的拉丁成分与真实的派生词族。

normal.en: Lis 'dispute' plus agere 'drive': litigate is driving a quarrel forward.
normal.cn: lis「争执」加 agere「驱动」：litigate 就是把争执往前推。

normal.en: Mitigate shares the driving verb but starts with mitis 'mild', so it means softening, not suing.
normal.cn: mitigate 共享「驱动」这个动词，但开头是 mitis「温和」，所以它指缓和，不是起诉。

normal.en: The family runs litigate, litigation, litigant, litigator and litigious.
normal.cn: 同族词有 litigate、litigation、litigant、litigator、litigious。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the choice: choose to litigate, threaten to litigate, litigate a dispute.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出这个选择：选择打官司、威胁起诉、就争议提起诉讼。

normal.en: Relitigate adds 'again', because courts keep records and repeats are visible.
normal.cn: relitigate 加了「再一次」，因为法院留有记录，重复是看得见的。

abstract.en: Picture a quarrel placed on rails and pushed, inch by inch, toward a distant bench.
abstract.cn: 想象一场口角被放上轨道，一寸一寸推向远处的高席。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked settlement on one side and court on the other: the verb is the hand that turns the second handle.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，一边写着和解，一边写着法院：这个动词就是转动第二个门把的那只手。

abstract.en: Picture the same word doing a small job for two people and a large job for a profession: one act, two scales.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词为两个人做一件小事，又为一个行业做一件大事：一个动作，两种尺度。

examples.en: The company decided to litigate rather than accept the penalty.
examples.cn: 公司决定打官司，而不是接受处罚。

examples.en: Only a small share of complaints are ever litigated.
examples.cn: 只有一小部分投诉真正进入了诉讼。

examples.en: They litigated over the ownership of a single wall for six years.
examples.cn: 他们为一堵墙的归属打了六年官司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立替门」——立了案，就得替自己一路守到门口 → 打官司

root: 拉丁 litigare（诉诸法院、争讼）= lis（争执）+ agere（驱动）；过去分词 litigatus。lis 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the plain act of going to court, through its target, its pleading, its choice against settlement, its professional use, repetition, wider campaigns and the old quarrel sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「去法院」这一基本动作开始，经它的对象、庭上争辩、与和解相对的选择、职业化使用、重复争讼、更大范围的推进，最后回到古老的「争吵」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quarrel put on rails and pushed toward a bench.
core.cn: 核心意象：一场口角被放上轨道，推向高席。

branches.en: THE MOVE: taking the dispute to court, and aiming it at a particular opponent.
branches.cn: 这一步：把争议送进法院，并把矛头对准特定对手。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: the push happens clause by clause, in speech before a judge.
branches.cn: 争辩：推力发生在一条条陈述里，在法官面前说出口。

branches.en: THE CHOICE: the same move is a refusal to settle, since a stranger will decide.
branches.cn: 选择：同一个动作意味着拒绝和解，因为将由陌生人裁决。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: repeating the move for clients turns it into a trade.
branches.cn: 职业：替当事人重复这个动作，它就成了一门行业。

branches.en: REPETITION AND WIDTH: the act can repeat, widen into a campaign, or shrink back to a plain quarrel.
branches.cn: 重复与宽窄：这个动作可以重复、扩展成一场运动，也可以缩回单纯的争吵。

intro.en: Litigate is a Latin verb stem with an English-derived family, so it is read as dispute plus driving plus endings.
intro.cn: litigate 是一个拉丁动词词干，带着一批英语派生词，读法是「争执」加「驱动」再加词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin lis supplies the noun of dispute and Latin agere the verb of driving; agere separately yields act, agent, agenda and exact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lis 提供争执名词，拉丁 agere 提供驱动动词；agere 另自衍生 act、agent、agenda、exact。

items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名争执本身。
这个动词命名那股推力。

items.structure: litigare (Latin verb) used unchanged in English
items.meaning: to carry a dispute through court
items.meaningCN: 把争议在法院里推到底（由拉丁动词原形直接进入英语，语义由「争吵」收窄为「诉讼」）
items.exampleCN: 任何一方都可以提起诉讼。

items.meaningCN: 诉讼这项活动（动作后缀把动词名词化）
替当事人打官司的人（施事后缀把动作变成人）

items.meaning: a party engaged in a case
items.meaningCN: 正在案中的一方（分词后缀把动作变成参与者）
爱打官司的（形容词后缀把动作变成倾向）
items.exampleCN: 好讼的文化会抬高成本。

items.meaning: to litigate the same issue once more
items.meaningCN: 就同一争点再打一次（重复前缀在动作上再加一轮）
items.example: The issue was relitigated last year.
items.exampleCN: 这一争点去年又打了一次。

latinEntries.meaning: having disputed, having gone to law
latinEntries.meaningCN: 已争讼的；已诉诸法院的
